bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第103卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 103
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 103

sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十五】起重光協洽，盡旃蒙大淵獻，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 25] From Chongguang Xieqia through Zhanmeng Dayuanxian, five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Records 25] Covering the five years from the cyclical year Chongguang-Xieqia (369) through Zhanmeng-Dayuanxian (373).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，袁瑾、朱輔求救於秦，秦王堅以瑾為揚州刺史，輔為交州刺史，遣武衛將軍武都王鑒、前將軍張蚝帥步騎二萬救之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yuan Jin and Zhu Fu sought rescue from Qin. King Fu Jian of Qin appointed Jin Governor of Yangzhou and Fu Governor of Jiaozhou, and sent Martial Guard General the Prince of Wudu Jian and Forward General Zhang Qie leading twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Yuan Jin and Zhu Fu appealed to Former Qin for help. King Fu Jian named Jin governor of Yangzhou and Fu governor of Jiaozhou, then dispatched the Martial Guard General, Prince of Wudu Wang Jian, and the Forward General Zhang Qie with twenty thousand foot and horse to their aid.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫遣淮南太守桓伊、南頓太守桓石虔等擊鑒、蚝於石橋，大破之，秦兵退屯慎城。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Huan Wen sent Huainan Administrator Huan Yi, Nandun Administrator Huan Shiqian, and others to attack Jian and Qie at Shiqiao, routing them utterly; the Qin troops withdrew and encamped at Shencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Huan Wen sent Huainan prefect Huan Yi, Nandun prefect Huan Shiqian, and others to strike Jian and Qie at Shiqiao. They won a crushing victory, and the Qin army fell back to Shencheng.

sentences.zh: 伊，宣之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yi was a son of Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，溫拔壽春。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, Wen captured Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: On the dinghai day, Huan Wen took Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 擒瑾及輔並其宗族，送建康斬之。

translations.literal: He captured Jin and Fu together with their clans, sent them to Jiankang, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yuan Jin and Zhu Fu along with their kinsmen, sent them to the capital at Jiankang, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅徙關東豪傑及雜夷十五萬戶於關中，處烏桓於馮翊、北地，丁零翟斌於新安、澠池。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin moved one hundred fifty thousand households of eastern-pass magnates and various aliens into Guanzhong, settling the Wuhuan in Fufeng and Beidi and the Dingling Zhai Bin in Xin'an and Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian relocated a hundred and fifty thousand households of eastern elites and non-Han peoples into the Guanzhong heartland, resettling the Wuhuan in Fufeng and Beidi and the Dingling leader Zhai Bin in Xin'an and Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 諸因亂流移、欲還舊業者，悉聽之。

translations.literal: All who had drifted away in the turmoil and wished to return to their former livelihoods were permitted to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone displaced by the wars who wished to go home and resume their former livelihood was allowed to do so.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦以魏郡太守韋鐘為青州刺史，中壘將軍梁成為兗州刺史，射聲校尉徐成為并州刺史，武衛將軍王鑒為豫州刺史，左將軍彭越為徐州刺史，太尉司馬皇甫覆為荊州刺史，屯騎校尉天水姜宇為涼州刺史，扶風內史王統為益州刺史，秦州刺史西縣侯雅為使持節、都督秦、晉、涼、雍州諸軍事、秦州牧，吏部尚書楊安為使持節、都督益、梁州諸軍事、梁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second month, Qin appointed Wei Commandery Administrator Wei Zhong Governor of Qingzhou, Central Rampart General Liang Cheng Governor of Yanzhou, She Sheng Commandant Xu Cheng Governor of Bingzhou, Martial Guard General Wang Jian Governor of Yuzhou, Left General Peng Yue Governor of Xuzhou, Grand Commandant's Major Huangfu Fu Governor of Jingzhou, Palace Cavalry Commandant Jiang Yu of Tianshui Governor of Liangzhou, Fufeng Interior Minister Wang Tong Governor of Yizhou, Qinzhou Governor Marquis Ya of Xixian as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Qin, Jin, Liang, and Yong provinces and Governor-General of Qinzhou, and Minister of the Civil Service Yang An as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Yi and Liang provinces and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Former Qin named Wei Zhong, prefect of Wei commandery, governor of Qingzhou; Liang Cheng, Central Rampart general, governor of Yanzhou; Xu Cheng, She Sheng commandant, governor of Bingzhou; Wang Jian, Martial Guard general, governor of Yuzhou; Peng Yue, Left general, governor of Xuzhou; Huangfu Fu, Grand Commandant's aide, governor of Jingzhou; Jiang Yu of Tianshui, Palace Cavalry commandant, governor of Liangzhou; Wang Tong, interior minister of Fufeng, governor of Yizhou; Marquis Ya of Xixian, governor of Qinzhou, bearer of the staff and commander over Qin, Jin, Liang, and Yong with the title Qinzhou governor-general; and Yang An, Minister of the Civil Service, bearer of the staff and commander over Yi and Liang as governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 復置雍州，治蒲阪；

translations.literal: Yongzhou was re-established, with its seat at Puban;
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou was restored, with its capital at Puban;

sentences.zh: 以長樂公丕為使持節、征東大將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: the Duke of Changle Pi was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: and the Duke of Changle Fu Pi was appointed bearer of the staff, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 成，平老之子；

translations.literal: Cheng was the son of Pinglao;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Cheng was a son of Liang Pinglao;

sentences.zh: 統，擢之子也。

translations.literal: Tong was the son of Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong was a son of Wang Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 堅以關東初平，守令宜得人，令王猛以便宜簡召英俊，補六州守令，授訖，言台除正。

translations.literal: Fu Jian, because the east had only just been pacified and prefects and magistrates needed capable men, ordered Wang Meng to select and summon outstanding talent at his discretion to fill the prefectural and county posts of the six provinces; once appointments were made, he was to report them to the central government for formal confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: With the east only just pacified, Fu Jian wanted the right men in local office. He told Wang Meng to recruit able men as he saw fit for the six provinces' prefects and magistrates, then report the appointments to the capital for formal ratification.

sentences.zh: 三月，壬辰，益州刺史建成定公周楚卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day renchen, Zhou Chu, Duke Ding of Jiancheng and Governor of Yizhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renchen, Zhou Chu, Duke Ding of Jiancheng and governor of Yizhou, died.

sentences.zh: 秦後將軍金城俱難攻蘭陵太守張閔子於桃山，大司馬溫遣兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: Qin's Rear General Ju Nan of Jincheng attacked Zhang Minzi, Administrator of Lanling, at Mount Tao; Grand Marshal Wen sent troops and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin's Rear General Ju Nan of Jincheng besieged Lanling prefect Zhang Minzi at Mount Tao. Huan Wen sent forces and repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 秦西縣侯雅、楊安、五統、徐成及羽林左監朱肜、揚武將軍姚萇帥步騎七萬伐仇池公楊纂。

translations.literal: Qin's Marquis Ya of Xixian, Yang An, Wang Tong, Xu Cheng, and the Left Inspector of the Feathered Forest Zhu Rong, together with Martial Valor General Yao Chang, led seventy thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the Duke of Chouchi Yang Zuan.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Ya of Xixian, Yang An, Wang Tong, Xu Cheng, Left Inspector of the Feathered Forest Zhu Rong, and Martial Valor General Yao Chang led seventy thousand foot and horse against Yang Zuan, Duke of Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 代將長孫斤謀弒代王什翼犍，世子寔格之，傷脅，遂執斤，殺之。

translations.literal: The Dai general Changsun Jin plotted to assassinate King Shiyijian of Dai; the heir apparent Shi blocked him, was wounded in the side, then seized Jin and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai general Changsun Jin plotted to murder King Shiyijian. The heir Shi intercepted him, took a wound in the side, seized Jin, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊午，大赦。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day wuwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on wuwu, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 秦兵至鷲峽，楊纂帥眾五萬拒之。

translations.literal: The Qin army reached Jiuxia; Yang Zuan led fifty thousand men to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin army reached Jiuxia Pass, where Yang Zuan met them with fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史弘農楊亮遣督護郭寶、卜靖帥千餘騎助纂，與秦兵戰於峽中；

translations.literal: Yang Liang of Hongnong, Governor of Liangzhou, sent Supervisors Guo Bao and Bu Jing leading more than a thousand cavalry to aid Zuan, and they fought the Qin army in the gorge;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang of Hongnong, governor of Liangzhou, sent Supervisors Guo Bao and Bu Jing with over a thousand horse to reinforce Zuan. They engaged the Qin forces in the gorge;

sentences.zh: 纂兵大敗，死者什三、四。

translations.literal: Zuan's army was utterly defeated; three or four tenths of the men died.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's army was routed, with thirty or forty percent killed.

sentences.zh: 寶等亦沒，纂收散兵遁還。

translations.literal: Bao and the others also perished; Zuan gathered the scattered troops and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and his men were lost as well. Zuan rallied the survivors and retreated.

sentences.zh: 西縣侯雅進攻仇池，楊統帥武都之眾降秦。

translations.literal: Marquis Ya of Xixian pressed the attack on Chouchi; Yang Tong led the people of Wudou in surrender to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Ya advanced on Chouchi, and Yang Tong brought the Wudou clans over to Qin.

sentences.zh: 纂懼，面縛出降，雅送纂於長安。

translations.literal: Zuan, in fear, bound himself and came out to surrender; Ya sent Zuan to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zuan came out with his hands bound. Ya sent him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以統為南秦州刺史；

translations.literal: Tong was made Governor of Southern Qinzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tong was appointed governor of Southern Qinzhou;

sentences.zh: 加楊安都督南秦州諸軍事，鎮仇池。

translations.literal: Yang An was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Southern Qinzhou and stationed at Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: and Yang An was made commander over Southern Qinzhou and posted at Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 王猛之破張天錫於枹罕也，獲其將敦煌陰據及甲士五千人。

translations.literal: When Wang Meng defeated Zhang Tianxi at Fuhan, he captured his general Yin Ju of Dunhuang and five thousand armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng defeated Zhang Tianxi at Fuhan, he took his general Yin Ju of Dunhuang and five thousand armored troops.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅既克楊纂，遣據帥其甲士還涼州，使著作郎梁殊、閻負送之，因命王猛為書諭天錫曰：「昔貴先公稱籓劉、石者，惟審於強弱也。

translations.literal: After King Fu Jian had conquered Yang Zuan, he sent Ju back to Liangzhou at the head of his armored troops, with Compilation Gentlemen Liang Shu and Yan Fu escorting them, and had Wang Meng write to instruct Tianxi, saying: "In former days your honored forebear submitted to Liu and Shi only because he judged strength and weakness aright.
translations.idiomatic: After subduing Yang Zuan, Fu Jian sent Ju back to Liangzhou at the head of his troops, with Compilation Gentlemen Liang Shu and Yan Fu as escorts, and had Wang Meng write to Tianxi: "Your distinguished ancestor once submitted to the Liu and Shi regimes because he read the balance of power correctly.

sentences.zh: 今論涼土之力，則損於往時；

translations.literal: If one speaks now of the power of the Liang lands, it is less than in former times;
translations.idiomatic: Today the Liang domain is weaker than it was then;

sentences.zh: 語大秦之德，則非二趙之匹；

translations.literal: if one speaks of Great Qin's virtue, it is not a match for the two Zhao states;
translations.idiomatic: while Great Qin's might is beyond anything the two Zhao states ever possessed;

sentences.zh: 而將軍翻然自絕，無乃非宗廟之福也歟！

translations.literal: yet the General abruptly cuts himself off—surely this is no blessing to the ancestral temple!
translations.idiomatic: yet you have abruptly cut yourself off from us—can that truly serve your ancestral house?

sentences.zh: 以秦之威，旁振無外，可以回弱水使東流，返江、河使西注。

translations.literal: With Qin's might shaking all without, one could turn the Ruoshui to flow east and send the Yangtze and Yellow rivers back west.
translations.idiomatic: With Qin's power reaching in every direction, we could turn the Ruoshui eastward and drive the Yangtze and Yellow rivers back to the west.

sentences.zh: 關東既平，將移兵河右，恐非六郡士民所能抗也。

translations.literal: With the east already pacified, troops will soon shift to the lands west of the river; I fear the people of the six commanderies cannot withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: The east is pacified; our armies will soon move west of the river, and the six commanderies' people and gentry can hardly stand against us.

sentences.zh: 劉表謂漢南可保，將軍謂西河可全，吉兇在身，元龜不遠，宜深算妙慮，自求多福，無使六世之業一旦而墜地也！」

translations.literal: Liu Biao thought the lands south of the Han could be held secure; the General thinks the western river can be kept whole—fortune and misfortune rest in one's own person, and the tortoise oracle is not far off. You should reckon deeply and plan wisely, seek your own good fortune, and not let the achievement of six generations fall to the ground in a single day!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao thought he could hold the Han southlands; you think you can keep the western river intact. Fortune and ruin are in your own hands, and the omens are plain. Plan carefully, secure your own advantage, and do not let six generations of achievement collapse in a day!"

sentences.zh: 天錫大懼，遣使謝罪稱籓。

translations.literal: Tianxi was greatly afraid and sent envoys to apologize and declare himself a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi was terrified and sent envoys to apologize and submit as a vassal.

sentences.zh: 堅拜天錫使持節、都督河右諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、涼州刺史、西平公。

translations.literal: Fu Jian appointed Tianxi Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs west of the river, Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Grandee with Bountiful Deeds Equal to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian confirmed Tianxi as bearer of the staff, commander over the west-of-the-river region, Rapid Cavalry grand general, Grandee of the First Rank, governor of Liangzhou, and Duke of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾王辟奚聞楊纂敗，五月，遣使獻馬千匹、金銀五百斤於秦。

translations.literal: When King Pixi of Tuyuhun heard that Yang Zuan had been defeated, in the fifth month he sent envoys presenting a thousand horses and five hundred jin of gold and silver to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of Yang Zuan's defeat, King Pixi of Tuyuhun sent envoys in the fifth month with a thousand horses and five hundred jin of gold and silver as tribute to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦以辟奚為安遠將軍、漒川侯。

translations.literal: Qin made Pixi Pacification-at-a-Distance General and Marquis of Qiangchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin named him Pacification-at-a-Distance General and Marquis of Qiangchuan.

sentences.zh: 辟奚，葉延之子也，好學，仁厚而無威斷。

translations.literal: Pixi was the son of Yeyan; he loved learning and was benevolent and generous but lacked stern decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Pixi, son of Yeyan, loved learning and was kind and humane, but he lacked firm authority.

sentences.zh: 三弟專恣，國人患之。

translations.literal: His three younger brothers were willful and overbearing, and the people of the state resented them.
translations.idiomatic: His three younger brothers were arrogant and domineering, and the people chafed under them.

sentences.zh: 長史鐘惡地，西漒羌豪也，謂司馬乞宿雲曰：「三弟縱橫，勢出王右，幾亡國矣。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk Zhong E'di, a Qiang magnate of the western Qiang, said to Major Qi Suyun: "The three younger brothers run rampant; their power exceeds the king's, and the state was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Zhong E'di, a western Qiang chieftain, said to Major Qi Suyun: "The three brothers run wild. Their power eclipses the king's, and the realm was nearly ruined.

sentences.zh: 吾二人位為元輔，豈得坐而視之！

translations.literal: We two hold the highest ministerial posts—how can we sit and watch!
translations.idiomatic: We two are chief ministers—how can we sit by and watch?

sentences.zh: 詰朝月望，文武並會，吾將討焉。

translations.literal: At dawn on the full moon, civil and military officials will assemble together, and I shall punish them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the next full moon, when civil and military officers gather, I will move against them.

sentences.zh: 王之左右皆吾羌子，轉目一顧，立可擒也。」

translations.literal: Those at the king's side are all our Qiang clansmen; at a turn of the eye they can be seized at once."
translations.idiomatic: The men at the king's side are all our Qiang kin. One glance from us and they can be seized on the spot."

sentences.zh: 宿雲請先白王，惡地曰：「王仁而無斷，白之必不從。

translations.literal: Suyun asked to inform the king first. E'di said: "The king is benevolent but indecisive; if we tell him, he will surely not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Suyun wanted to inform the king first. E'di said: "The king is humane but cannot decide. Tell him and he will refuse.

sentences.zh: 萬一事洩，吾屬無類矣。

translations.literal: If by any chance the matter leaks out, our kind will be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: If word leaks out, none of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 事已出口，何可中變！」

translations.literal: The matter is already spoken—how can it be changed midway!"
translations.idiomatic: The plan is spoken. There is no turning back now!"

sentences.zh: 遂於坐收三弟，殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the gathering he seized the three younger brothers and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: At the assembly he seized the three brothers and killed them.

sentences.zh: 辟奚驚怖，自投床下，惡地、宿雲趨而扶之曰：「臣昨夢先王刺臣雲：『三弟將為逆，不可不討。』

translations.literal: Pixi, terrified, threw himself under the bed; E'di and Suyun hurried forward to support him and said: "Your servant dreamed last night that the late king stabbed your servant Yun, saying: 'The three younger brothers will rebel; they must be punished.'
translations.idiomatic: Pixi, terrified, threw himself under the bed. E'di and Suyun rushed to help him up and said: "Last night your servant dreamed the late king rebuked Yun: 'The three brothers will rebel. You must not spare them.'

sentences.zh: 故誅之耳。」

translations.literal: That is why they were executed."
translations.idiomatic: That is why we executed them."

sentences.zh: 辟奚由是發病恍惚，命世子視連曰：「吾禍及同生，何以見之於地下！

translations.literal: Thereupon Pixi fell ill in a daze. He charged the heir Shilian, saying: "I have brought disaster on my own brothers—how can I face them in the underworld!
translations.idiomatic: Pixi then fell ill, his mind clouded. He told the heir Shilian: "I have harmed my own brothers. How can I face them in the grave!

sentences.zh: 國事大小，任汝治之，吾餘年殘命，寄食而已。」

translations.literal: Great and small affairs of state—leave them to you to govern. My remaining years are but a borrowed life, living on others' food alone."
translations.idiomatic: Great matters and small, leave them to you. My few remaining years are nothing but borrowed breath."

sentences.zh: 遂以憂卒。

translations.literal: He then died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He died of grief soon after.

sentences.zh: 視連立，不飲酒游畋者七年，軍國之事，委之將佐。

translations.literal: Shilian succeeded to the throne; for seven years he did not drink wine or go hunting or hawking, and military and state affairs he entrusted to his generals and aides.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian succeeded him. For seven years he neither drank wine nor went hunting, leaving military and civil affairs to his officers.

sentences.zh: 鐘惡地諫，以為：「人主當自娛樂，建威布德。」

translations.literal: Zhong E'di remonstrated, saying: "A ruler ought to enjoy himself, establish authority, and spread virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong E'di admonished him: "A ruler should take his pleasures, build his authority, and spread his virtue."

sentences.zh: 視連泣曰：「孤自先世以來，以仁孝忠恕相承。

translations.literal: Shilian wept and said: "From our forebears down, benevolence, filial piety, loyalty, and forbearance have been handed on in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Shilian wept and said: "From our forebears we have handed down benevolence, filial piety, loyalty, and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 先王念友愛之不終，悲憤而亡。

translations.literal: The late king, brooding that brotherly love was not sustained to the end, died in grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: My father could not keep brotherly love to the end and died in grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 孤雖纂業，屍存而已，聲色游娛，豈所安也！

translations.literal: Though I have succeeded to the enterprise, I am but a living corpse—how could music, women, and diversions bring me peace!
translations.idiomatic: Though I hold the throne, I am a living corpse. How could pleasure and sport bring me peace!

sentences.zh: 威德之建，當付之將來耳。」

translations.literal: The building of authority and virtue must be left to the future."
translations.idiomatic: Authority and virtue must wait for another day."

sentences.zh: 代世子寔病傷而卒。

translations.literal: The Dai heir apparent Shi died of his wound.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai heir Shi died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，秦王堅如洛陽。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, King Fu Jian of Qin went to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, King Fu Jian went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 代世子寔娶東部大人賀野干之女，有遺腹子，甲戌，生男，代王什翼犍為之赦境內，名曰涉圭。

translations.literal: The Dai heir Shi had married the daughter of the eastern chieftain He Yegan; she bore a posthumous son. On the day jiaxu a boy was born, and King Shiyijian of Dai proclaimed an amnesty within the realm and named him Shegui.
translations.idiomatic: The late heir Shi had married the daughter of the eastern chieftain He Yegan, who was pregnant at his death. On jiaxu she bore a son. King Shiyijian amnestied the realm and named the child Shegui.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫以梁、益多寇，周氏世有威名，八月，以寧州刺史周仲孫監益、梁二州諸軍事，領益州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen, because Liang and Yi had many raiders and the Zhou clan had long borne a name for authority, in the eighth month made Zhou Zhongsun, Governor of Ningzhou, Overseer of military affairs in Yi and Liang provinces and acting Governor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits plaguing Liang and Yi and the Zhou clan renowned for military prestige, Huan Wen in the eighth month made Ningzhou governor Zhou Zhongsun overseer of Yi and Liang and acting governor of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 仲孫，光之子也。

translations.literal: Zhongsun was the son of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhongsun was a son of Zhou Guang.

sentences.zh: 秦以光祿勳李儼為河州刺史，鎮武始。

translations.literal: Qin appointed Li Yan, Household Master of the Imperial Heir, Governor of Hezhou and stationed him at Wushi.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin named Li Yan, Household Master of the Heir Apparent, governor of Hezhou and posted him at Wushi.

sentences.zh: 王猛以潞川之功，請以鄧羌為司隸。

translations.literal: Wang Meng, for the achievement at Luchuan, requested that Deng Qiang be made Director of the Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: For the victory at Luchuan, Wang Meng asked that Deng Qiang be made Director of the Retainers.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅下詔曰：「司隸校尉，董牧皇畿，吏責甚重，非所以優禮名將。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian issued an edict saying: "The Director of the Retainers supervises the imperial capital region; the burden of office is very heavy and is not the way to honor a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian decreed: "The Director of the Retainers governs the capital region. Its duties are heavy and it is no way to honor a famous general.

sentences.zh: 光武不以吏事處功臣，實貴之也。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu did not burden his meritorious ministers with clerical duties—he truly valued them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu kept his great ministers out of petty administration—that was how he honored them.

sentences.zh: 羌有廉、李之才，朕方委以征伐之事，北平匈奴，南蕩揚、越，羌之任也，司隸何足以嬰之！

translations.literal: Qiang has the talent of Lian Po and Li Mu. I am about to entrust him with campaigns—pacifying the Xiongnu in the north and sweeping Yang and Yue in the south. That is Qiang's charge; how could the Directorship suffice to bind him!
translations.idiomatic: Qiang has the gifts of Lian Po and Li Mu. I mean to give him campaigns—subduing the Xiongnu in the north and clearing Yang and Yue in the south. That is his task. The Directorship is far too small to hold him!

sentences.zh: 其進號鎮軍將軍，位特進。」

translations.literal: Let his title be advanced to Pacifying-the-Army General with rank of Special Advancement."
translations.idiomatic: Promote him to Pacifying-the-Army General with Special Advancement rank."

sentences.zh: 九月，秦王堅還長安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, King Fu Jian returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fu Jian returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 歸安元侯李儼卒於上邽，堅復以儼子辯為河州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Yan, Marquis Yuan of Gui'an, died at Shanggui; Fu Jian again appointed Yan's son Bian Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, Marquis Yuan of Gui'an, died at Shanggui. Fu Jian named his son Bian governor of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，秦王堅如鄴，獵於西山，旬餘忘返。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, King Fu Jian went to Ye, hunted on the Western Hills, and for more than ten days forgot to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter Fu Jian went to Ye and hunted in the Western Hills, staying away for more than ten days.

sentences.zh: 伶人王洛叩馬諫曰：「陛下群生所系，今久獵不歸，一旦患生不虞，奈太后、天下何！」

translations.literal: The entertainer Wang Luo knocked on the horse and remonstrated, saying: "Your Majesty is what all living beings depend on. Now you hunt long and do not return; if illness or mishap should arise without warning, what of the Empress Dowager and the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: The performer Wang Luo seized the bridle and remonstrated: "Your Majesty holds the fate of all the people. You have hunted too long. If some sudden illness should strike, what will become of the Empress Dowager and the realm?"

sentences.zh: 堅為之罷獵還宮。

translations.literal: Fu Jian for this reason ended the hunt and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian ended the hunt and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 王猛因進言曰：「畋獵誠非急務，王洛之言，不可忘也。」

translations.literal: Wang Meng then advanced and said: "Hunting is truly no urgent business; Wang Luo's words must not be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng added: "Hunting is no urgent matter. Do not forget what Wang Luo said."

sentences.zh: 堅賜洛帛百匹，拜官箴左右，自是不復獵。

translations.literal: Fu Jian gave Luo a hundred bolts of silk, appointed him Admonisher at the Left of the court, and from then on did not hunt again.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian gave Luo a hundred bolts of silk, made him Admonisher on the Left, and never hunted again.

sentences.zh: 大司馬溫恃其材略位望，陰蓄不臣之志，嘗撫枕歎曰：「男子不能流芳百世，亦當遺臭萬年！」

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Wen, relying on his talent, strategy, position, and prestige, secretly harbored ambitions of disloyalty. He once stroked his pillow and sighed: "If a man cannot leave a fragrant name for a hundred generations, he should at least leave a stench for ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Trusting in his talent, rank, and prestige, Grand Marshal Huan Wen secretly nursed treasonous designs. Once he stroked his pillow and sighed: "If a man cannot leave a good name for a hundred generations, let him leave an infamous one for ten thousand!"

sentences.zh: 術士杜炅能知人貴賤，溫問炅以己祿位所至，炅曰：「明公勳格宇宙，位極人臣。」

translations.literal: The diviner Du Jiong could tell men's high and low station. Wen asked Jiong how far his rank and emolument would reach. Jiong said: "My lord's merit fills the cosmos; your position is the utmost among ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Du Jiong could read a man's rank. Huan Wen asked how high he would rise. Jiong said: "My lord's merit fills heaven and earth. You stand at the summit of subjecthood."

sentences.zh: 溫不悅。

translations.literal: Wen was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen was displeased.

sentences.zh: 溫欲先立功河朔，以收時望，還受九錫。

translations.literal: Wen wished first to establish merit north of the Yellow River, win the esteem of the age, and then return to receive the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted first to win glory north of the Yellow River, regain public esteem, and then receive the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 及枋頭之敗，威名頓挫。

translations.literal: When he was defeated at Fangtou, his prestige was suddenly shattered.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Fangtou his prestige collapsed.

sentences.zh: 既克壽春，謂參軍郗超曰：「足以雪枋頭之恥乎？」

translations.literal: After he had taken Shouchun, he said to his aide Xi Chao: "Is this enough to wash away the shame of Fangtou?"
translations.idiomatic: After taking Shouchun he asked his aide Xi Chao: "Is this enough to wipe away the shame of Fangtou?"

sentences.zh: 超曰：「未也。」

translations.literal: Chao said: "Not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Chao said: "Not yet."

sentences.zh: 久之，超就溫宿，中夜，謂溫曰：「明公都無所慮乎？」

translations.literal: After some time Chao lodged with Wen; at midnight he said to Wen: "My lord, have you no concerns at all?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Chao stayed the night with Huan Wen. At midnight he said: "My lord, are you not worried at all?"

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「卿欲有言邪？」

translations.literal: Wen said: "Do you wish to speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said: "Do you have something to say?"

sentences.zh: 超曰：「明公當天下重任，今以六十之年，敗於大舉，不建不世之勳，不足以鎮愜民望！」

translations.literal: Chao said: "My lord bears the great burden of the realm. Now at sixty years, after defeat in a major campaign, if you do not achieve a transcendent merit, it will not suffice to steady and satisfy the people's expectations!"
translations.idiomatic: Chao said: "You bear the realm's weight. At sixty, after a great defeat, unless you win a supreme achievement you cannot steady the people's hopes!"

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「然則奈何？」

translations.literal: Wen said: "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said: "What then should I do?"

sentences.zh: 超曰：「明公不為伊、霍之舉者，無以立大威權，鎮壓四海。」

translations.literal: Chao said: "Unless my lord performs the act of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, you cannot establish great authority and awe and suppress the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: Chao said: "Unless you do as Yi Yin and Huo Guang did, you cannot build supreme authority and rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 溫素有心，深以為然，遂與之定議。

translations.literal: Wen had long harbored such intent and deeply agreed; he then settled the plan with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had long harbored such designs and agreed wholeheartedly. They settled on a plan.

sentences.zh: 以帝素謹無過，而床第易誣，乃言「帝早有痿疾，嬖人相龍、計好、朱炅寶等，參侍內寢，二美人田氏、孟氏生三男，將建儲立王，傾移皇基。」

translations.literal: Because the emperor had always been careful and without fault, but the bedchamber is easy to slander, they said: "The emperor long had impotence; favorites Xiang Long, Ji Hao, Zhu Lingbao, and others attended him in the inner apartments; two beauties of the Tian and Meng clans bore three sons and were about to establish an heir and set up a prince, overturning the imperial foundation."
translations.idiomatic: “The emperor had always been scrupulous and without fault, but bedroom matters are easy to slander. They spread word that he had long been impotent, that favorites Xiang Long, Ji Hao, and Zhu Lingbao attended him in the inner chambers, that two concubines of the Tian and Meng clans had borne three sons, and that they meant to name an heir and overturn the dynasty.”

sentences.zh: 密播此言於民間，時人莫能審其虛實。

translations.literal: They secretly spread this talk among the people, and at the time none could judge whether it was true or false.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly spread this story among the people, and no one could tell truth from lie.

sentences.zh: 十一月，癸卯，溫自廣陵將還姑孰，屯於白石。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day guimao, Wen was about to return from Guangling to Gudu and encamped at Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on guimao, Huan Wen was returning from Guangling to Gudu and encamped at Baishi.

sentences.zh: 丁未，詣建康，諷褚太后，請廢帝，立丞相會稽王昱，並作令草呈之。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei he went to Jiankang, hinted to Empress Dowager Chu, and requested that the emperor be deposed and Chancellor the Prince of Kuaiji Yu be enthroned; he also drafted an edict and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he went to Jiankang, pressed Empress Dowager Chu to depose the emperor and enthrone Chancellor Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, and presented a draft edict.

sentences.zh: 太后方在佛屋燒香，內侍啟雲：「外有急奏。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was just burning incense in the Buddhist hall when a palace attendant announced: "There is an urgent memorial outside."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was burning incense in the Buddhist chapel when an attendant announced: "There is an urgent memorial outside."

sentences.zh: 太后出，倚戶視奏數行，乃曰：「我本自疑此！」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager came out, leaned against the door and read a few lines of the memorial, then said: "I had myself suspected this!"
translations.idiomatic: She came out, leaned against the door, read a few lines, and said: "I had suspected as much myself!"

sentences.zh: 至半，便止，索筆益之曰：「未亡人不幸罹此百憂，感念存沒，心焉如割。」

translations.literal: When she had read halfway, she stopped, asked for a brush and added: "This surviving widow has unhappily suffered these hundred griefs; thinking of the living and the dead, my heart is as if cut apart."
translations.idiomatic: Halfway through she stopped, asked for a brush, and added: "This widow has suffered grief upon grief. Thinking of the living and the dead, my heart is torn."

sentences.zh: 己酉，溫集百官於朝堂。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Wen assembled all officials in the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Huan Wen assembled the officials in the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 廢立既曠代所無，莫有識其故典者，百官震心栗。

translations.literal: Deposing and enthroning was something no age had seen; none knew the old precedents, and all the officials were shaken and trembling at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing and enthroning an emperor was unprecedented. No one knew the old rites, and every official was terrified.

sentences.zh: 溫亦色動，不知所為。

translations.literal: Wen too changed color and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen himself turned pale and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射王彪之知事不可止，乃謂溫曰：「公阿衡皇家，當倚傍先代。」

translations.literal: Wang Biaozhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, knew the affair could not be stopped and said to Wen: "My lord, as pillar and balance of the imperial house, you should rely on former ages."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, knew the matter could not be halted. He told Huan Wen: "You are the pillar of the royal house. Follow the precedents of old."

sentences.zh: 乃命取《霍光傳》，禮度儀制，定於須臾。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Biography of Huo Guang brought; rites, measures, and ceremonial forms were settled in a moment.
translations.idiomatic: He had the Biography of Huo Guang brought, and within moments the rites and protocol were settled.

sentences.zh: 彪之朝服當階，神彩毅然，曾無懼容。

translations.literal: Biaozhi in court dress stood at the steps; his spirit was stern and resolute, and he showed not the least fear.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi stood on the steps in court dress, stern and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 文武儀准，莫不取定，朝廷以此服之。

translations.literal: Civil and military ceremonial standards—none were not taken from his determinations, and the court for this reason respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Every detail of civil and military ceremony was settled by him, and the court admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 於是宣太后令，廢帝為東海王，以丞相、錄尚書事、會稽王昱統承皇極。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Empress Dowager's order was proclaimed: the emperor was deposed as Prince of Donghai, and Chancellor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Prince of Kuaiji Yu was to succeed to the imperial foundation.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's edict was read: the emperor was deposed as Prince of Donghai, and Chancellor Sima Yu, Prince of Kuaiji, was to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 百官入太極前殿，溫使督護竺瑤、散騎侍郎劉亨收帝璽綬。

translations.literal: The officials entered the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; Wen sent Supervisors Zhu Yao and Gentlemen-Attendant Liu Heng to take the emperor's seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: The officials entered the Hall of Supreme Ultimate. Huan Wen sent Zhu Yao and Liu Heng to take the imperial seal and cord.

sentences.zh: 帝著白帢單衣，步下西堂，乘犢車出神虎門，群臣拜辭，莫不歔欷。

translations.literal: The emperor wore a white kerchief and single garment, walked down from the western hall, rode a calf-drawn cart out through the Shenhu Gate; the officials bowed in farewell, and all sob.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wore a white cap and plain robe, walked down from the western hall, and rode out through the Shenhu Gate in an ox cart. The officials bowed in farewell, weeping.

sentences.zh: 侍御史、殿中監將兵百人衛送東海第。

translations.literal: The Attendant Censor and Palace Director led a hundred soldiers to escort him to the Donghai residence.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant censor and palace director escorted him with a hundred troops to the Donghai residence.

sentences.zh: 溫帥百官具乘輿法駕，迎會稽王於會稽邸。

translations.literal: Wen led the officials with the imperial carriage and full regalia to welcome the Prince of Kuaiji at the Kuaiji residence.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen led the officials with the imperial carriage and full regalia to welcome the Prince of Kuaiji at his residence.

sentences.zh: 王於朝堂變服，著平巾幘、單衣，東向流涕，拜受璽綬，是日，即皇帝位，改元。

translations.literal: The prince changed dress in the audience hall, put on a plain kerchief cap and single garment, faced east weeping, bowed and received the seal and cord; that same day he took the imperial throne and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: At the audience hall the prince changed clothes, put on a plain cap and robe, faced east in tears, and bowed to receive the seal and cord. That day he took the throne and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 溫出次中堂，分兵屯衛。

translations.literal: Wen went out and lodged in the central hall, dividing troops to garrison and guard.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen withdrew to the central hall and posted troops as guards.

sentences.zh: 溫有足疾，詔乘輿入殿。

translations.literal: Wen had an ailment of the foot; an edict allowed him to ride the imperial carriage into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had a foot ailment and was permitted to ride the imperial carriage into the hall.

sentences.zh: 溫撰辭，欲陳述廢立本意，帝引見，便泣下數十行，溫兢懼，竟不能一言而出。

translations.literal: Wen prepared a speech wishing to set forth the true intent of the deposition and enthronement; the emperor summoned him, and at once tears streamed down in dozens of lines. Wen was fearful and cautious and in the end could not speak a single word before leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had prepared a speech explaining why he deposed and enthroned emperors. When the new emperor received him, tears streamed down his face. Huan Wen was terrified and left without saying a word.

sentences.zh: 太宰武陵王晞，好習武事，為溫所忌，欲廢之，以事示王彪之。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor, Prince of Wuling Xi, loved military exercises and was resented by Wen, who wished to depose him and showed the matter to Wang Biaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Xi, Prince of Wuling, loved military affairs. Huan Wen resented him and wanted him removed. He showed his plan to Wang Biaozhi.

sentences.zh: 彪之曰：「武陵親尊，未有顯罪，不可以猜嫌之間便相廢徙。

translations.literal: Biaozhi said: "Wuling is close in kin and high in honor; he has no manifest crime—one cannot on the basis of suspicion and resentment simply depose and banish him.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi said: "The Prince of Wuling is close kin and of high rank. He has committed no clear crime. You cannot remove him on mere suspicion.

sentences.zh: 公建立聖明，當崇獎王室，與伊、周同美；

translations.literal: My lord has established a sage and enlightened ruler; you ought to honor and encourage the royal house and share the glory of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: You have enthroned a worthy ruler. You should honor the royal house and match the fame of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 此大事，宜更深詳。」

translations.literal: this is a great matter and should be considered more deeply and carefully."
translations.idiomatic: this is a grave matter and deserves far more thought."

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「此已成事，卿勿復言！」

translations.literal: Wen said: "This is already settled—do not speak of it again!"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said: "It is already decided. Say no more!"

sentences.zh: 乙卯，溫表「晞聚納輕剽，息綜矜忍；

translations.literal: On the day yimao Wen memorialized: "Xi gathers and accepts the reckless and light; his son Zong is proud and cruel;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Huan Wen memorialized that Xi "gathers reckless men, and his son Zong is proud and cruel;

sentences.zh: 袁真叛逆，事相連染。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen's rebellion involved them by connection.
translations.idiomatic: their affairs were linked to Yuan Zhen's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 頃日猜懼，將成亂階。

translations.literal: Recently suspicion and fear have nearly become the steps to disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Recent suspicion and fear were about to breed rebellion.

sentences.zh: 請免晞官，以王歸籓。」

translations.literal: I request that Xi's offices be removed and that he, as prince, return to his fief."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that his offices be removed and that he return to his fief as a prince."

sentences.zh: 從之，並免其世子綜、梁王□逢等官。

translations.literal: This was approved, and the offices of his heir Zong, Prince of Liang [Feng], and others were also removed.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and also removed the offices of his heir Zong, the Prince of Liang, and others.

sentences.zh: 溫使魏郡太守毛安之帥所領宿衛殿中。

translations.literal: Wen sent Mao Anzhi, Administrator of Wei Commandery, to lead his personal guard in garrisoning the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen sent Wei prefect Mao Anzhi to garrison the palace with his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 安之，虎生之弟也。

translations.literal: Anzhi was the younger brother of Husheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Anzhi was a younger brother of Mao Husheng.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，尊褚太后曰崇德太后。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Empress Dowager Chu was honored as Empress Dowager Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Empress Dowager Chu was honored as Empress Dowager Chongde.

sentences.zh: 初，殷浩卒，大司馬溫使人□書吊之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yin Hao died, Grand Marshal Wen sent someone with a letter of condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yin Hao died, Grand Marshal Huan Wen sent a letter of condolence.

sentences.zh: 浩子涓不答，亦不詣溫，而與武陵王晞游。

translations.literal: Hao's son Juan did not reply, nor did he go to Wen, but associated with Prince of Wuling Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's son Juan did not reply and did not visit Huan Wen, but kept company with Prince Xi of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史庾蘊，希之弟也，素與溫有隙。

translations.literal: Yu Yun, Governor of Guangzhou, was the younger brother of Xi and had long had a rift with Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yun, governor of Guangzhou, was the younger brother of Yu Xi and had long been at odds with Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫惡殷、庾宗強，欲去之。

translations.literal: Wen hated the strength of the Yin and Yu clans and wished to remove them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen hated the power of the Yin and Yu clans and wanted them eliminated.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，使其弟祕逼新蔡王晃詣西堂叩頭自列，稱與晞及子綜、著作郎殷涓、太宰長史庾倩、掾曹秀、捨人劉強、散騎常侍庾柔等謀反；

translations.literal: On the day xinhai he had his brother Mi force Prince Huang of Xincai to go to the western hall, knock his head and confess himself, saying that he had plotted rebellion with Xi and his son Zong, Compilation Gentleman Yin Juan, Grand Tutor's Chief Clerk Yu Qian, Clerk Cao Xiu, Attendant Liu Qiang, Regular Attendant Yu Rou, and others;
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he had his brother Mi force Prince Huang of Xincai to the western hall to confess that he had plotted rebellion with Xi, Zong, Yin Juan, Yu Qian, Cao Xiu, Liu Qiang, Yu Rou, and others;

sentences.zh: 帝對之流涕，溫皆收付廷尉。

translations.literal: the emperor wept facing him, and Wen had them all taken and handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor wept at the confession, and Huan Wen had them all sent to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 倩、柔，皆蘊之弟也。

translations.literal: Qian and Rou were both younger brothers of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Rou were both younger brothers of Yu Yun.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，溫殺東海王三子及其母。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Wen killed the three sons of the Prince of Donghai and their mother.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Huan Wen killed the three sons of the deposed emperor and their mother.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，御史中丞譙王恬承溫旨，請依律誅武陵王晞。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin, Wang Tian, Prince of Qiao and Attending Censor-in-Chief, following Wen's intent, requested that Prince Xi of Wuling be executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Wang Tian, Prince of Qiao and censor-in-chief, at Huan Wen's bidding asked that Prince Xi of Wuling be executed under the law.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「悲惋惶怛，非所忍聞，況言之哉！

translations.literal: An edict said: "Grief, regret, and dread—this is not what I can bear to hear, let alone speak of!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor decreed: "Grief and dread—this I cannot bear to hear, let alone speak of!

sentences.zh: 其更詳議！」

translations.literal: Let there be further detailed deliberation!"
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate further!"

sentences.zh: 恬，承之孫也。

translations.literal: Tian was the grandson of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tian was a grandson of Wang Cheng.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，溫重表固請誅晞，詞甚酷切。

translations.literal: On the day yimao Wen again memorialized, firmly requesting Xi's execution; his language was very harsh and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Huan Wen memorialized again, insisting on Xi's execution in the harshest terms.

sentences.zh: 帝乃賜溫手詔曰：「若晉祚靈長，公便宜奉行前詔；

translations.literal: The emperor then gave Wen a handwritten edict saying: "If Jin's mandate is long-lived, my lord may conveniently carry out the former edict;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Huan Wen a handwritten note: "If Jin's mandate endures, you may carry out the earlier edict;

sentences.zh: 如其大運去矣，請避賢路。」

translations.literal: if its great destiny is gone, please yield the path to the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: if its great destiny is spent, please yield the path to worthier men."

sentences.zh: 溫覽之，流汗變色，乃奏廢晞及三子，家屬皆徙新安郡。

translations.literal: Wen read it, sweated and changed color, and then memorialized to depose Xi and his three sons; all their families were banished to Xin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen read it, broke into a sweat, and memorialized instead to depose Xi and his three sons. Their families were exiled to Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，免新蔡王晃為庶人，徙衡陽；

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Prince Huang of Xincai was reduced to commoner and banished to Hengyang;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Prince Huang of Xincai was reduced to commoner status and exiled to Hengyang;

sentences.zh: 殷涓、庾倩、曹秀、劉強、庾柔皆族誅，庾蘊飲鴆死。

translations.literal: Yin Juan, Yu Qian, Cao Xiu, Liu Qiang, and Yu Rou were all executed to the third degree of kinship; Yu Yun drank poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Juan, Yu Qian, Cao Xiu, Liu Qiang, and Yu Rou were executed with their clans. Yu Yun took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 蘊兄東陽太守友子婦，桓豁之女也，故溫特赦之。

translations.literal: Yun's elder brother You, Administrator of Dongyang—his son's wife was the daughter of Huan Huo, and for this reason Wen specially pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's brother You, Dongyang prefect, had a daughter-in-law who was Huan Huo's daughter, so Huan Wen pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 庾希聞難，與弟會稽王參軍邈及子攸之逃於海陵陂澤中。

translations.literal: Yu Xi, hearing of the disaster, fled with his younger brother Miao, military aide to the Prince of Kuaiji, and his son Youzhi to the marshes and lakes of Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi, hearing of the purge, fled with his brother Miao and his son Youzhi into the marshes of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 溫既誅殷、庾，威勢翕赫，侍中謝安見溫遙拜。

translations.literal: After Wen had executed the Yin and Yu clans, his authority blazed; Palace Attendant Xie An, seeing Wen, bowed from afar.
translations.idiomatic: After eliminating the Yin and Yu clans, Huan Wen's power was overwhelming. Palace Attendant Xie An bowed to him from a distance.

sentences.zh: 溫驚曰：「安石，卿何事乃爾？」

translations.literal: Wen said in surprise: "Anshi, why do you act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said in surprise: "Anshi, why do you bow from so far away?"

sentences.zh: 安曰：「未有君拜於前，臣揖於後。」

translations.literal: An said: "Never yet has the lord bowed in front while the minister salutes from behind."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An said: "Never yet has the lord bowed in front while the minister salutes from behind."

sentences.zh: 戊午，大赦，增文武位二等。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed and civil and military ranks were raised two grades.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu a general amnesty was declared and civil and military ranks were raised two grades.

sentences.zh: 己未，溫如白石，上書求歸姑孰。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Wen went to Baishi and submitted a memorial requesting to return to Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Huan Wen went to Baishi and asked to return to Gudu.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔進溫丞相，大司馬如故，留京師輔政；

translations.literal: On the day gengshen an edict advanced Wen to Chancellor while keeping him Grand Marshal as before, to remain in the capital to assist in government;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict made Huan Wen chancellor while retaining him as Grand Marshal, to remain at the capital as regent;

sentences.zh: 溫固辭，仍請還鎮。

translations.literal: Wen firmly declined and still requested to return to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen firmly declined and asked to return to his post.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，溫自白石還姑孰。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Wen returned from Baishi to Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Huan Wen returned from Baishi to Gudu.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅聞溫廢立，謂群臣曰：「溫前敗灞上，後敗枋頭，不能思愆自貶以謝百姓，方更廢君以自說，六十之叟，舉動如此，將何以自容於四海乎！

translations.literal: When King Fu Jian of Qin heard of Wen's deposition and enthronement, he said to his ministers: "Wen was first defeated at Bashang, then at Fangtou; he could not reflect on his faults and humble himself to apologize to the people, but instead deposed the ruler to justify himself—a man of sixty acting thus—how will he face the four seas!
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian heard of Huan Wen's coup, he told his ministers: "Huan Wen lost at Bashang and Fangtou. Instead of repenting before the people, he deposed an emperor to justify himself. A man of sixty behaving thus—how can he face the world?

sentences.zh: 諺曰：『怒其室而作色於父。』

translations.literal: A proverb says: 'Angry at one's wife but showing one's temper to one's father.'
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says: 'Angry at one's wife but taking it out on one's father.'

sentences.zh: 其桓溫之謂矣。」

translations.literal: Is this not said of Huan Wen?"
translations.idiomatic: That fits Huan Wen."

sentences.zh: 秦車騎大將軍王猛，以六州任重，言於秦王堅，請改授親賢；

translations.literal: Wang Meng, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry of Qin, because the six provinces' burden was heavy, spoke to King Fu Jian and requested reassignment to a kinsman or worthy;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, Qin's Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, told Fu Jian the six provinces were too heavy a burden and asked to hand them to a kinsman or worthy man;

sentences.zh: 及府選便宜，輒已停寢，別乞一州自效。

translations.literal: and as for the provincial selections at his discretion, he had already suspended them, separately requesting one province in which to prove his service.
translations.idiomatic: he had already halted discretionary appointments and asked instead for a single province where he could serve.

sentences.zh: 堅報曰：「朕之於卿，義則君臣，親逾骨肉，雖復桓、昭之有管、樂，玄德之有孔明，自謂逾之。

translations.literal: Fu Jian replied: "Between you and me, in righteousness we are ruler and minister, in closeness we exceed flesh and bone. Though Duke Huan and Duke Zhao had Guan and Yue, and Xuande had Kongming, I consider myself to surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian replied: "Between us, you are my minister and more than kin. Duke Huan and Duke Zhao had Guan Zhong and Yue Yi; Liu Bei had Zhuge Liang. I think I surpass them all in you.

sentences.zh: 夫人主勞於求才，逸於得士。

translations.literal: A ruler toils in seeking talent and rests once he has obtained a worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler toils to find talent and rests once he has found a worthy man.

sentences.zh: 既以六州相委，則朕無東顧之憂，非所以為優崇，乃朕自求安逸也。

translations.literal: Having entrusted you with the six provinces, I have no worry of looking east—this is not to honor and exalt you, but for me to seek ease myself.
translations.idiomatic: Entrusting you with six provinces frees me from worry in the east. This is not to honor you but to give myself peace.

sentences.zh: 夫取之不易，守之亦難，苟任非其人，患生慮表，豈獨朕之憂，亦卿之責也，故虛位台鼎而以分陝為先。

translations.literal: To take is not easy, to hold is also hard; if the wrong man is appointed, trouble arises beyond expectation—is it only my worry? It is your responsibility too. Therefore I leave the Tripod posts vacant and put the partition of Shaan first.
translations.idiomatic: Winning territory is hard; holding it is harder. Appoint the wrong man and trouble follows—not mine alone but yours as well. That is why I leave the highest posts empty and put the eastern provinces first.

sentences.zh: 卿未照朕心，殊乖素望。

translations.literal: You have not understood my heart and greatly fall short of my long-held hopes.
translations.idiomatic: You do not understand my heart and fall far short of what I hoped.

sentences.zh: 新政俟才，宜速銓補；

translations.literal: The new administration awaits talent; you should quickly examine and fill posts;
translations.idiomatic: The new administration needs men. Appoint them quickly;

sentences.zh: 俟東方化洽，當袞衣西歸。」

translations.literal: when the east is transformed and harmonized, I shall don the imperial robes and return west."
translations.idiomatic: when the east is pacified I shall return west in imperial robes."

sentences.zh: 仍遣侍中梁讜詣鄴諭旨，猛乃視事如故。

translations.literal: He then sent Palace Attendant Liang Chan to Ye to convey the intent, and Meng resumed his duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Palace Attendant Liang Chan to Ye with his message, and Wang Meng resumed his duties as before.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大司馬溫奏：「廢放之人，屏之以遠，不可以臨黎元。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Grand Marshal Wen memorialized: "A deposed and banished person should be screened far away and cannot be allowed near the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Grand Marshal Huan Wen memorialized: "A deposed ruler must be kept far from the people.

sentences.zh: 東海王宜依昌邑故事，築第吳郡。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai should follow the precedent of Changyi and have a residence built in Wu Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Donghai should follow the Changyi precedent and be housed in Wu commandery."

sentences.zh: 太后詔曰：「使為庶人，情有不忍，可特封王。」

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's edict said: "To make him a commoner—my feelings cannot bear it; he may be specially enfeoffed as a prince."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager decreed: "I cannot bear to reduce him to commoner status. Enfeoff him as a prince instead."

sentences.zh: 溫又奏：「可封海西縣侯。」

translations.literal: Wen again memorialized: "He may be enfeoffed as Marquis of Haixi County."
translations.idiomatic: “Huan Wen memorialized again that he be made Marquis of Haixi.”

sentences.zh: 庚寅，封海西縣公。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin he was enfeoffed as Duke of Haixi County.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he was enfeoffed as Duke of Haixi.

sentences.zh: 溫威振內外，帝雖處尊位，拱默而已，常懼廢黜。

translations.literal: Wen's authority shook within and without; though the emperor occupied the honored position, he only folded his hands in silence and constantly feared deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's power shook court and country. The emperor sat in silence and lived in fear of deposition.

sentences.zh: 先是，熒惑守太微端門，逾月而海西廢。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mars had lingered at the Terminal Gate of the Supreme Palace; after more than a month the Prince of Haixi was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mars had lingered at the Terminal Gate of the Supreme Palace constellation; a month later the Prince of Haixi was deposed.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，熒惑逆行入太微，帝甚惡之。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, Mars moved retrograde into the Supreme Palace; the emperor greatly dreaded it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Mars moved retrograde into the Supreme Palace. The emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎郗超在直，帝謂超曰：「命之修短，本所不計，故當無復近日事邪？」

translations.literal: Xi Chao, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, was on duty; the emperor said to Chao: "The length or shortness of fate I do not reckon—but surely there will be no repeat of recent events?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi Chao of the Masters of Writing was on duty. The emperor said to him: "I do not count my days—but surely nothing like recent events will happen again?"

sentences.zh: 超曰：「大司馬臣溫，方內固社稷，外恢經略，非常之事，臣以百口保之。」

translations.literal: Chao said: "Grand Marshal, your minister Wen, is now securing the altars of state within and expanding strategy without—extraordinary matters I guarantee with the lives of a hundred mouths."
translations.idiomatic: Chao said: "Grand Marshal Huan Wen is securing the realm within and expanding our frontiers. I stake the lives of my whole clan that nothing extraordinary will happen."

sentences.zh: 及超請急省其父，帝曰：「致意尊公，家國之事，遂至於此，由吾不能以道匡衛，愧歎之深，言何能諭！」

translations.literal: When Chao asked leave to visit his father urgently, the emperor said: "Convey my regards to your honored father. State and family have come to this because I could not uphold the Way and guard them—my shame and sighs are so deep that words cannot express them!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chao asked leave to visit his father, the emperor said: "Give your father my regards. State and family have come to this because I could not uphold the Way. My shame is too deep for words."

sentences.zh: 因詠庾闡詩雲：「志士痛朝危，忠臣哀主辱。」

translations.literal: He then recited a poem of Yu Chan: "Men of purpose grieve when the court is in peril; loyal ministers mourn when the ruler is shamed."
translations.idiomatic: He then recited Yu Chan's lines: "Men of purpose grieve when the court is in peril; loyal ministers mourn when the ruler is shamed."

sentences.zh: 遂泣下沾襟。

translations.literal: Tears then soaked his robe.
translations.idiomatic: Tears soaked his robe.

sentences.zh: 帝美風儀，善容止，留心典籍，凝塵滿席，湛如也。

translations.literal: The emperor had fine bearing and deportment, attended to the classics; dust lay thick on his mat, yet he was serene.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had fine bearing and grace, loved the classics, and sat serene though dust lay thick on his mat.

sentences.zh: 雖神識恬暢，然無濟世大略，謝安以為惠帝之流，但清談差勝耳。

translations.literal: Though his spirit was tranquil and at ease, he had no grand strategy to save the age; Xie An considered him of the type of Emperor Hui, only somewhat better at pure talk.
translations.idiomatic: His mind was calm but he lacked a statesman's vision. Xie An ranked him with Emperor Hui of Jin—only somewhat better at pure talk.

sentences.zh: 郗超以溫故，朝中皆畏事之。

translations.literal: Because of his connection with Wen, everyone at court feared and deferred to Xi Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his tie to Huan Wen, everyone at court feared Xi Chao.

sentences.zh: 謝安嘗與左衛將軍王坦之共詣超，日旰未得前，坦之欲去，安曰：「獨不能為性命忍須臾邪？」

translations.literal: Xie An once went with Left Guard General Wang Tanzhi to visit Chao; the sun set and they still had not been received. Tanzhi wished to leave; An said: "Can you not endure a moment for the sake of your life?"
translations.idiomatic: Xie An once went with Left Guard General Wang Tanzhi to visit Chao. Sunset came and they still had not been admitted. Tanzhi wanted to leave. An said: "Cannot you endure a moment for your life's sake?"

sentences.zh: 秦以河州刺史李辯領興晉太守，還鎮枹罕。

translations.literal: Qin made Li Bian, Governor of Hezhou, also Administrator of Xingjin and returned him to garrison Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin made Hezhou governor Li Bian also prefect of Xingjin and posted him back to Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 徙涼州治金城。

translations.literal: The seat of Liangzhou was moved to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Liangzhou capital was moved to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 張天錫聞秦有兼併之志，大懼，立壇於姑臧南，刑三牲。

translations.literal: Zhang Tianxi, hearing that Qin harbored designs of annexation, was greatly afraid; he set up an altar south of Guzang and sacrificed the three animals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tianxi, hearing Qin meant to annex him, was terrified. He set up an altar south of Guzang and sacrificed the three sacrificial animals.

sentences.zh: 帥其官屬，遙與晉三公盟。

translations.literal: He led his officials in alliance from afar with the Three Dukes of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He led his officials in a distant alliance with the Three Excellencies of Jin.

sentences.zh: 遣從事中郎韓博奉表送盟文，並獻書於大司馬溫，期以明年夏同大舉，會於上邽。

translations.literal: He sent Attendant Gentleman Han Bo to present a memorial delivering the alliance text and also a letter to Grand Marshal Wen, fixing the next summer for a joint great campaign to meet at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Attendant Gentleman Han Bo with the alliance text and a letter to Grand Marshal Huan Wen, proposing a joint campaign the next summer at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 是歲，秦益州刺史王統攻隴西鮮卑乞伏司繁於度堅山，司繁帥騎三萬拒統於苑川。

translations.literal: That year, Wang Tong, Governor of Yizhou in Qin, attacked the Xianbei of Longxi, Qifu Sifan, at Mount Dujian; Sifan led thirty thousand cavalry to resist Tong at Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qin Yizhou governor Wang Tong attacked the Longxi Xianbei leader Qifu Sifan at Mount Dujian. Sifan met him at Yuanchuan with thirty thousand horse.

sentences.zh: 統潛襲度堅山，司繁部落五萬餘皆降於統；

translations.literal: Tong secretly attacked Mount Dujian, and more than fifty thousand of Sifan's tribesmen all surrendered to Tong;
translations.idiomatic: Tong secretly struck Mount Dujian, and more than fifty thousand of Sifan's tribesmen surrendered;

sentences.zh: 其眾聞妻子已降秦，不戰而潰。

translations.literal: his troops, hearing that their wives and children had already surrendered to Qin, collapsed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: his army, hearing their families had surrendered to Qin, fled without a fight.

sentences.zh: 司繁無所歸，亦詣統降。

translations.literal: Sifan had nowhere to go and also went to Tong to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: With nowhere left to turn, Qifu Sifan also went to Wang Tong and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以司繁為南單于，留之長安；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin made Sifan Southern Chanyu and kept him at Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian named Sifan Southern Chanyu and kept him at Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 以司繁從叔吐雷為勇士護軍，撫其部眾。

translations.literal: he made Sifan's younger cousin by the father's side, Tulei, Protector of the Army of Brave Warriors to pacify his tribesmen.
translations.idiomatic: he appointed Sifan's paternal cousin Tulei Protector of the Army of Brave Warriors to govern his followers.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，秦以清河房曠為尚書左丞，征曠兄默及清河崔逞、燕國韓胤為尚書郎，北平陽陟、田勰、陽瑤為著作佐郎，郝略為清河相，皆關東士望，王猛所薦也。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, Qin appointed Fang Kuo of Qinghe as Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, summoned Kuo's elder brother Mo together with Cui Cheng of Qinghe and Han Yin of Yan as Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing, Yang Zhi of Beiping, Tian Xie, and Yang Yao as Assistant Gentlemen of Compilation, and Hao Lue as Administrator of Qinghe—all were leading men of the eastern passes, recommended by Wang Meng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, Former Qin made Fang Kuo of Qinghe Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and summoned his elder brother Mo, Cui Cheng of Qinghe, and Han Yin of Yan as Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing. Yang Zhi of Beiping, Tian Xie, and Yang Yao were made Assistant Gentlemen of Compilation, and Hao Lue was made prefect of Qinghe. All were leading eastern gentry, recommended by Wang Meng.

sentences.zh: 瑤，騖之子也。

translations.literal: Yao was the son of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yao was a son of Yang Wu.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍慕容垂言於秦王堅曰：「臣叔父評，燕之惡來輩也，不宜復污聖朝，願陛下為燕戮之。」

translations.literal: Champion General Murong Chui said to King Fu Jian of Qin: "My uncle Ping is of the same breed as Yan's E Lai; he ought not again to stain the sacred court. I beg Your Majesty to execute him on Yan's behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Murong Chui said to King Fu Jian: "My uncle Murong Ping is another E Lai of Yan. He should not stain your court again. I beg Your Majesty to put him to death for Yan's sake."

sentences.zh: 堅乃出評為范陽太守，燕之諸王悉補邊郡。

translations.literal: Fu Jian then sent Ping out as Administrator of Fanyang, and all the princes of Yan were posted to frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian instead sent Murong Ping out as prefect of Fanyang and posted all the Yan princes to frontier commanderies.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：古之人，滅人之國而人悅，何哉？

translations.literal: Minister Guang said: The men of old destroyed others' states yet the people rejoiced—why?
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: Why did the ancients destroy kingdoms and still win the people's hearts?

sentences.zh: 為人除害故也。

translations.literal: Because they removed harm for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Because they removed the people's scourges.

sentences.zh: 彼慕容評者，蔽君專政，忌賢疾功，愚闇貪虐，以喪其國，國亡不死，逃遁見擒。

translations.literal: That Murong Ping blinded his ruler and monopolized power, envied the worthy and hated merit, was stupid, dark, greedy, and cruel, and thereby lost his state; when the state perished he did not die but fled and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping had blinded his ruler and seized power, envied talent and resented achievement, and ruled with stupidity, greed, and cruelty until he lost the kingdom. When Yan fell he did not die but fled and was taken.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅不以為誅首，又從而寵秩之，是愛一人而不愛一國之人也，其失人心多矣。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin did not take his head but instead favored and enfeoffed him—this was loving one man and not loving the people of a whole state; how greatly he lost men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian did not execute him but instead honored and enfeoffed him. That was cherishing one man and not cherishing a whole kingdom's people. He lost hearts in abundance.

sentences.zh: 是以施恩於人而人莫之恩，盡誠於人而人莫之誠。

translations.literal: Thus though he showed kindness to men, none returned kindness; though he gave full sincerity to men, none returned sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: So when he showed kindness, none felt grateful; when he gave his full sincerity, none gave theirs in return.

sentences.zh: 卒於功名不遂，容身無所，由不得其道故也。

translations.literal: At last his merit and fame were not fulfilled and he had nowhere to shelter himself—because he did not hold to the right Way.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his ambitions failed and he had nowhere to stand—because he did not follow the right Way.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊年，遣侍中王坦之征大司馬溫入輔，溫復辭。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day wushen, Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi was sent to summon Grand Marshal Wen to enter and assist at court; Wen again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the wushen day, Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi was sent to summon Grand Marshal Huan Wen to court. Wen declined again.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅詔：「關東之民學通一經，才成一藝者，在所郡縣以禮送之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin decreed: "Among the people of the eastern passes, those who have mastered one classic or achieved skill in one art shall, in their commanderies and counties, be sent forward with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian decreed: "In the eastern passes, anyone who has mastered one classic or achieved skill in one art shall be sent forward with ceremony from his commandery or county.

sentences.zh: 在官百石以上，學不通一經，才不成一藝者，罷遣還民。」

translations.literal: Officials of one hundred shi of salary and above who have not mastered one classic or achieved skill in one art shall be dismissed and returned to the people."
translations.idiomatic: Any official drawing a hundred shi or more who has not mastered one classic or achieved skill in one art shall be dismissed and sent back to private life."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，徙海西公於吳縣西柴裡，敕吳國內史刁彝防衛，又遣御史顧允監察之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Prince of Haixi was moved to Xichaili in Wuxian; the Interior Minister of Wu, Diao Yi, was ordered to guard him, and Censor Gu Yun was also sent to supervise him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer the Prince of Haixi was moved to Xichaili in Wuxian. Diao Yi, interior minister of Wu, was ordered to guard him, and Censor Gu Yun was sent to oversee him.

sentences.zh: 彝，協之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yi was a son of Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸酉，秦以王猛為丞相、中書監、尚書令、太子太傅、司隸校尉，特進、常侍、持節、將軍、侯如故；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day guiyou, Qin made Wang Meng Chancellor, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Director of the Masters of Writing, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and Colonel of the Retainers, with Special Advance, Regular Attendant, Bearer of the Staff, General, and Marquis unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the guiyou day, Former Qin made Wang Meng chancellor, supervisor of the Masters of Writing, director of the Masters of Writing, grand tutor of the heir apparent, and colonel of the retainers, retaining his special advance, regular attendant, staff of authority, generalship, and marquisate;

sentences.zh: 陽平公融為使持節、都督六州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、冀州牧。

translations.literal: the Duke of Yangping, Rong, was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in the six provinces, Grand General Who Guards the East, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: and the Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in six provinces, Grand General Who Guards the East, and governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 庾希、庾邈與故青州刺史武沈之子遵，聚眾夜入京口城，晉陵太守卞眈逾城奔曲阿。

translations.literal: Yu Xi, Yu Miao, and Zun, son of the former Governor of Qingzhou Wu Shen, gathered troops and by night entered Jingkou city; Jingling Administrator Bian Dan climbed over the wall and fled to Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi, Yu Miao, and Wu Zun, son of the former Qingzhou governor Wu Shen, gathered men and entered Jingkou by night. Jingling prefect Bian Dan fled over the wall to Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 希詐稱受海西公密旨誅大司馬溫。

translations.literal: Xi falsely claimed to have received a secret order from the Prince of Haixi to execute Grand Marshal Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xi falsely claimed a secret order from the Prince of Haixi to kill Grand Marshal Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 建康震擾，內外戒嚴。

translations.literal: Jiankang was shaken and alarmed; within and without martial law was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang was thrown into alarm, and martial law was declared inside and out.

sentences.zh: 卞眈發諸縣兵二千人擊希，希敗，閉城自守。

translations.literal: Bian Dan raised two thousand troops from the counties and attacked Xi; Xi was defeated and shut the city to hold out.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Dan raised two thousand county troops and attacked Xi. Xi was beaten back and shut himself in the city.

sentences.zh: 溫遣東海內史周少孫討之。

translations.literal: Wen sent Donghai Interior Minister Zhou Shaosun to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen sent Donghai interior minister Zhou Shaosun to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬辰，拔其城，擒希、邈及其親黨，皆斬之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renchen, the city was taken; Xi, Miao, and their close associates were captured and all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the renchen day, the city was taken. Xi, Miao, and their associates were captured and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 眈，壺之子也。

translations.literal: Dan was the son of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Dan was a son of Bian Hu.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，帝不豫，急召大司馬溫入輔，一日一夜發四詔。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin the emperor fell ill and urgently summoned Grand Marshal Wen to enter and assist; in one day and one night four edicts were issued.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiayin day the emperor fell ill and urgently summoned Grand Marshal Huan Wen to court. Four edicts went out in a single day and night.

sentences.zh: 溫辭不至。

translations.literal: Wen declined and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen declined and did not come.

sentences.zh: 初，帝為會稽王，娶王述從妹為妃，生世子道生及弟俞生。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Prince of Kuaiji, he took Wang Shu's younger female cousin by the father's side as consort and begot the heir Daosheng and his younger brother Yusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when he was Prince of Kuaiji, the emperor married Wang Shu's younger female cousin and had the heir Daosheng and a younger son, Yusheng.

sentences.zh: 道生疏躁無行，母子皆以幽廢死。

translations.literal: Daosheng was coarse, rash, and without conduct; mother and son both died after being confined and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng was coarse and ill-behaved. He and his mother were both confined and died in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 餘三子，郁、朱生、天流，皆早夭。

translations.literal: Three other sons—Yu, Zhusheng, and Tianliu—all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Three other sons—Yu, Zhusheng, and Tianliu—all died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 諸姬絕孕將十年，王使善相者視之，皆曰：「非其人。」

translations.literal: The concubines had ceased to conceive for nearly ten years; the prince had skilled physiognomists examine them, and all said: "Not the right person."
translations.idiomatic: The concubines had borne no children for nearly ten years. The prince sent physiognomists to examine them, and all said: "Not the one."

sentences.zh: 又使視諸婢媵，有李陵容者，在織坊中，黑而長，宮人謂之「崑崙」，相者驚曰：「此其人也！」

translations.literal: He then had them examine the maids and attendants; there was one named Li Lingrong, in the weaving quarters, dark and tall, whom the palace women called "Kunlun"; the physiognomist started and said: "This is the one!"
translations.idiomatic: Then they examined the maids. One named Li Lingrong worked in the weaving quarters—dark-skinned and tall, nicknamed "Kunlun" by the palace women. The physiognomist exclaimed: "This is the one!"

sentences.zh: 王召之侍寢，生子昌明及道子。

translations.literal: The prince summoned her to his bed and she bore Changming and Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: The prince took her to his bed. She bore Changming and Daozi.

sentences.zh: 己未，立昌明為皇太子，生十年矣。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei Changming was established as heir apparent; he was ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day Changming was made heir apparent. He was ten years old.

sentences.zh: 以道子為琅邪王，領會稽國，以奉帝母鄭太妃之祀。

translations.literal: Daozi was made Prince of Langye and put in charge of the Kingdom of Kuaiji to maintain the sacrifices to the emperor's mother, Consort Dowager Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi was made Prince of Langye and given charge of Kuaiji to maintain the sacrifices to Consort Dowager Zheng, the emperor's mother.

sentences.zh: 遺詔：「大司馬溫依周公居攝故事。」

translations.literal: The death edict said: "Grand Marshal Wen shall follow the precedent of the Duke of Zhou acting as regent."
translations.idiomatic: The death edict read: "Grand Marshal Huan Wen shall follow the Duke of Zhou's precedent as regent."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「少子可輔者輔之，如不可，君自取之。」

translations.literal: It also said: "If the younger son can be assisted, assist him; if not, take the throne yourself."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "If the younger son can be guided, guide him. If not, take the throne yourself."

sentences.zh: 侍中王坦之自持詔入，於帝前毀之。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi took the edict in himself and tore it up before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi brought the edict in and tore it up before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下，儻來之運，卿何所嫌！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The realm is a fortune that came by chance—what do you find objectionable!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The realm is fortune that came by chance—what do you object to!"

sentences.zh: 坦之曰：「天下，宣、元之天下，陛下何得專之！」

translations.literal: Tanzhi said: "The realm is the realm of Emperor Xuan and Emperor Yuan—how can Your Majesty dispose of it alone!"
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi said: "The realm belongs to Emperors Xuan and Yuan. How can Your Majesty dispose of it alone!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃使坦之改詔曰：「家國事一稟大司馬，如諸葛武侯、王丞相故事。」

translations.literal: The emperor then had Tanzhi revise the edict to read: "State and family affairs shall all be referred to the Grand Marshal, following the precedents of Martial Marquis Zhuge and Chancellor Wang."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Tanzhi rewrite the edict: "State and family affairs shall all be referred to the Grand Marshal, as under Zhuge Liang and Wang Dao."

sentences.zh: 是日，帝崩。

translations.literal: That day the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 群臣疑惑，未敢立嗣，或曰：「當須大司馬處分。」

translations.literal: The ministers were uncertain and did not dare establish the successor; some said: "We must wait for the Grand Marshal's decision."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers hesitated and dared not proclaim a successor. Some said: "We must wait for the Grand Marshal's decision."

sentences.zh: 尚書僕射王彪之正色曰：「天子崩，太子代立，大司馬何容得異！

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Biaozhi said sternly: "When the Son of Heaven dies, the heir succeeds—how can the Grand Marshal presume to differ!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Biaozhi said sternly: "When the Son of Heaven dies, the heir succeeds. How can the Grand Marshal presume otherwise!

sentences.zh: 若先面咨，必反為所責。」

translations.literal: If we consult him first, we will instead be blamed by him."
translations.idiomatic: If we consult him first, he will turn and blame us."

sentences.zh: 朝議乃定。

translations.literal: Court deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The court's decision was made.

sentences.zh: 太子即皇帝位，大赦。

translations.literal: The heir took the imperial throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The heir took the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 崇德太后令，以帝沖幼，加在諒闇，令溫依周公居攝故事。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Chongde issued an order that, because the emperor was young and still in mourning seclusion, Wen should follow the precedent of the Duke of Zhou acting as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Chongde ordered that, because the emperor was young and still in mourning, Huan Wen should follow the Duke of Zhou's precedent as regent.

sentences.zh: 事已施行，王彪之曰：「此異常大事，大司馬必當固讓，使萬機停滯，稽廢山陵，未敢奉令，謹具封還。」
