translations.literal: The matter had already been put into effect when Wang Biaozhi said: "This is an extraordinary matter; the Grand Marshal will surely firmly decline, causing all affairs of state to stall and delaying the imperial tomb—I dare not accept the order and respectfully seal and return it."
translations.idiomatic: The order had already gone out when Wang Biaozhi said: "This is an extraordinary matter. The Grand Marshal will surely refuse, stalling all affairs of state and delaying the imperial tomb. I dare not accept the order and respectfully return it sealed."

sentences.zh: 事遂不行。

translations.literal: The matter then did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The matter went no further.

sentences.zh: 溫望簡文臨終禪位於己，不爾便當居攝。

translations.literal: Wen had hoped that Emperor Jianwen on his deathbed would abdicate the throne to him; if not, he should at least act as regent.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen had hoped Emperor Jianwen would abdicate to him on his deathbed; failing that, he expected to serve as regent.

sentences.zh: 既不副所望，甚憤怨，與弟沖書曰：「遺詔使吾依武侯、王公故事耳。」

translations.literal: When this did not match his hopes he was greatly angry and resentful; he wrote to his younger brother Chong: "The death edict only makes me follow the precedents of Martial Marquis and Chancellor Wang."
translations.idiomatic: When his hopes were dashed he was furious. He wrote his younger brother Huan Chong: "The death edict only makes me follow Zhuge Liang and Wang Dao."

sentences.zh: 溫疑王坦之、謝安所為，心銜之。

translations.literal: Wen suspected Wang Tanzhi and Xie An of doing this and nursed resentment in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen suspected Wang Tanzhi and Xie An and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 詔謝安征溫入輔，溫又辭。

translations.literal: An edict through Xie An summoned Wen to enter and assist; Wen again declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict through Xie An summoned Huan Wen to court. Wen declined again.

sentences.zh: 八月，秦丞相猛至長字，復加都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Qin Chancellor Meng arrived at Chang'an and was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Former Qin chancellor Wang Meng reached Chang'an and was additionally made commander of all military affairs within and without.

sentences.zh: 猛辭曰：「元相之重，儲傅之尊，端右事繁，京牧任大，總督戎機，出納帝命，文武兩寄，鉅細並關，以伊、呂、蕭、鄧之賢，尚不能兼，況臣猛之無似！」

translations.literal: Meng declined, saying: "The weight of Chancellor, the honor of Grand Tutor to the heir, the many duties of the right-hand director, the great charge of capital governor, overall command of military affairs, receiving and issuing the emperor's commands—civil and military burdens together, great and small all involved—even the worthies Yi Yin, Lü Shang, Xiao He, and Deng Yu could not combine these; how much less one like me, Meng!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng declined: "The chancellor's weight, the heir's tutor's honor, the director's many duties, the capital governor's charge, command of military affairs, and receipt of the emperor's orders—civil and military together, great and small alike—even Yi Yin, Lü Shang, Xiao He, and Deng Yu could not combine all this. How much less could I!"

sentences.zh: 章三四上，秦王堅不許，曰：「朕方混壹四海，非卿誰可委者？

translations.literal: He submitted memorials three or four times; King Fu Jian of Qin would not permit it and said: "I am now unifying the four seas—besides you, to whom can I entrust this?
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized three or four times. King Fu Jian refused and said: "I am unifying the realm—besides you, to whom can I entrust it?

sentences.zh: 卿之不得辭宰相，猶朕不得辭天下也。」

translations.literal: That you cannot decline the chancellorship is like my not being able to decline the realm."
translations.idiomatic: That you cannot decline the chancellorship is like my not being able to decline the realm."

sentences.zh: 猛為相，堅端拱於上，成官總己於下，軍國內外之事，無不由之。

translations.literal: When Meng became chancellor, Fu Jian sat with folded hands above while officials below gathered affairs to themselves; matters of army and state within and without all passed through him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Meng became chancellor, Fu Jian sat above with folded hands while officials below deferred to Meng. Every matter of army and state passed through him.

sentences.zh: 猛剛明清肅，善惡著白，放黜屍素，顯拔幽滯，勸課農桑，練習軍旅，官必當才，刑必當罪。

translations.literal: Meng was firm, bright, and austere; good and evil stood out clearly; he dismissed the idle and promoted the obscure and blocked; he urged farming and sericulture and drilled the armies; offices must match talent, punishments must match crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng was firm, clear, and austere. Good and evil stood out plainly. He dismissed the idle, promoted the overlooked, urged farming, and drilled the armies. Office went to the capable; punishment fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 由是國富兵強，戰無不克，秦國大治。

translations.literal: Thereby the state grew rich and the army strong; in battle none went unconquered, and Qin was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: The state grew rich and the army strong. In battle they were unbeaten. Qin was brought to good order.

sentences.zh: 堅敕太子宏及長樂公丕等曰：「汝事王公，如事我也。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian instructed the heir Hong and the Duke of Changle Pi and others: "Serve Lord Wang as you serve me."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian told the heir Hong, the Duke of Changle Fu Pi, and the others: "Serve Lord Wang as you serve me."

sentences.zh: 陽平公融在冀州，高選綱紀，以尚書郎房默、河間相申紹為治中別駕，清河崔宏為州從事，管記室。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yangping, Rong, was in Jizhou and carefully selected his staff, making Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Fang Mo and Administrator of Hejian Shen Shao his Chief and Vice Directors, Cui Hong of Qinghe as Secretariat Attendant of the province in charge of the record office.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, was in Jizhou and carefully chose his staff. He made Gentleman of the Masters of Writing Fang Mo and Hejian prefect Shen Shao his chief and vice directors, and Cui Hong of Qinghe provincial secretariat attendant in charge of the record office.

sentences.zh: 融年少，為政好新奇，貴苛察；

translations.literal: Rong was young and in governing loved novelty, valuing harsh scrutiny;
translations.idiomatic: Rong was young and loved novelty in government, prizing harsh scrutiny;

sentences.zh: 申紹數規正，導以寬和，融雖敬之，未能盡從。

translations.literal: Shen Shao repeatedly corrected and guided him toward leniency and harmony; though Rong respected him, he could not fully follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shao repeatedly corrected him and urged leniency. Rong respected him but did not fully follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 後紹出為濟北太守，融屢以過失聞，數致譴讓，乃自恨不用紹言。

translations.literal: Later Shao went out as Administrator of Jibei; Rong was repeatedly heard of for faults and often received reprimands, and then regretted not having taken Shao's words.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shen Shao was posted out as prefect of Jibei. Rong was repeatedly reported for faults and often reprimanded, and then regretted not having listened to Shen Shao.

sentences.zh: 融嘗坐擅起學捨為有司所糾，遣主簿李纂詣長安自理；

translations.literal: Rong was once impeached by the authorities for having built a schoolhouse on his own authority and sent his Chief Clerk Li Zuan to Chang'an to plead his case;
translations.idiomatic: Rong was once impeached for building a schoolhouse on his own authority and sent his chief clerk Li Zuan to Chang'an to plead his case;

sentences.zh: 纂憂懼，道卒。

translations.literal: Zuan was anxious and afraid and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zuan was stricken with fear and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 融問申紹：「誰可使者？」

translations.literal: Rong asked Shen Shao: "Who can be sent?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong asked Shen Shao: "Who can be sent?"

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「燕尚書郎高泰，清辯有膽智，可使也。」

translations.literal: Shao said: "Gao Tai, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Yan, is clear in argument and has courage and wit—he can be sent."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said: "Gao Tai, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing of Yan, is clear-spoken, brave, and clever. He can go."

sentences.zh: 先是丞相猛及融屢辟泰，泰不起；

translations.literal: Earlier Chancellor Meng and Rong had repeatedly summoned Tai, but Tai would not rise to office;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chancellor Wang Meng and Rong had repeatedly summoned Gao Tai, but he had refused;

sentences.zh: 至是，融謂泰曰：「君子救人之急，卿不得復辭！」

translations.literal: at this time Rong said to Tai: "A gentleman saves men in urgent need—you cannot decline again!"
translations.idiomatic: now Rong told Gao Tai: "A gentleman answers a man's urgent need. You cannot refuse again!"

sentences.zh: 泰乃從命。

translations.literal: Tai then obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tai then obeyed.

sentences.zh: 至長安，丞相猛見之，笑曰：「高子伯於今乃來，何其遲也！」

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, Chancellor Meng saw him and laughed: "Gao Zibo has come at last—how late!"
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an Chancellor Wang Meng received him and laughed: "Gao Zibo has come at last. How late!"

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「罪人來就刑，何問遲速！」

translations.literal: Tai said: "A guilty man comes to accept punishment—why ask whether late or early!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tai said: "A guilty man comes to accept punishment. Why ask whether I am late or early!"

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: Meng said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng said: "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「昔魯僖公以泮宮發頌，劉宣王以稷下垂聲。

translations.literal: Tai said: "Formerly Duke Xi of Lu raised a hymn from the Pan Palace, and King Xuan of Liu won fame beneath the Ji altar.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tai said: "Duke Xi of Lu won praise for founding the Pan Palace school. King Xuan of Liu won fame for the Ji altar.

sentences.zh: 今陽平公開建學宮，追蹤劉、魯，未聞明詔褒美，乃更煩有司舉劾。

translations.literal: Now the Duke of Yangping openly built a school palace, following in the tracks of Liu and Lu, yet no clear edict of praise was heard; instead the authorities were further troubled to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Duke of Yangping openly built a school, following Liu and Lu, yet no clear edict praised him. Instead the authorities were set to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 明公阿衡聖朝，懲勸如此，下吏何所逃其罪乎！」

translations.literal: Your Excellency balances the sacred court—if reward and punishment are like this, how can lower officials escape guilt!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Excellency steadies the sacred court. If reward and punishment work like this, how can a lower official escape blame!"

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「是吾過也。」

translations.literal: Meng said: "This is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng said: "That is my fault."

sentences.zh: 事遂得釋。

translations.literal: The matter was then released.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 猛因歎曰：「高子伯豈陽平所宜吏乎！」

translations.literal: Meng then sighed and said: "Is Gao Zibo really an officer fit for Yangping!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng sighed: "Is Gao Zibo really an officer for Yangping!"

sentences.zh: 言於秦王堅。

translations.literal: He spoke of this to King Fu Jian of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke of this to King Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 堅召見，悅之，問以為治之本，對曰：「治本在得人，得人在審舉，審舉在核真，未有官得其人而國家不治者也。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian summoned and received him, was pleased with him, and asked about the root of good government; he replied: "The root of governance lies in getting the right men; getting men lies in careful selection; careful selection lies in verifying truth—never has a state been ill governed when offices had the right men."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian summoned him, was pleased, and asked the root of good government. Gao Tai replied: "The root of governance is getting the right men. Getting men depends on careful selection. Careful selection depends on verifying truth. No state with the right men in office has ever failed to prosper."

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「可謂辭簡而理博矣。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "One may say the words are brief yet the principle is broad."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said: "Brief words, broad principle."

sentences.zh: 以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was made Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 秦固請還州，堅許之。

translations.literal: Tai firmly requested to return to the province; Fu Jian permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tai firmly asked to return to the province, and Fu Jian agreed.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲寅，追尊故會稽王妃王氏曰順皇後，尊帝母李氏為淑妃。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jiayin, the former consort of the Prince of Kuaiji, Lady Wang, was posthumously honored as Empress Shun, and the emperor's mother Lady Li was honored as Shufei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the jiayin day, the former consort of the Prince of Kuaiji, Lady Wang, was posthumously honored as Empress Shun, and the emperor's mother Lady Li was made Shufei.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯，葬簡文帝於高平陵。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day dingmao, Emperor Jianwen was buried at Gaoping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the dingmao day, Emperor Jianwen was buried at Gaoping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 彭城妖人盧悚自稱大道祭酒，事之者八百餘家。

translations.literal: Lu Song, a sorcerer of Pengcheng, called himself Libationer of the Great Way; more than eight hundred households followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Song, a sorcerer of Pengcheng, called himself Libationer of the Great Way. More than eight hundred households followed him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，遣弟子許龍如吳，晨，到海西公門，稱太后密詔，奉迎興復；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he sent his disciple Xu Long to Wu; in the morning he reached the gate of the Prince of Haixi, claiming a secret edict of the empress dowager to welcome and restore him;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he sent his disciple Xu Long to Wu. At dawn Xu Long reached the Prince of Haixi's gate, claiming a secret empress dowager edict to welcome and restore him;

sentences.zh: 公初欲從之，納保母諫而止。

translations.literal: the prince at first wished to follow but, accepting his nurse's remonstrance, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: the prince at first meant to go along but stopped when his nurse remonstrated with him.

sentences.zh: 龍曰：「大事垂捷，焉用兒女子言乎！」

translations.literal: Long said: "The great affair is on the verge of success—why heed women's words!"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Long said: "The great affair is nearly won—why heed a woman's words!"

sentences.zh: 公曰：「我得罪於此，幸蒙寬宥，豈敢妄動！

translations.literal: The prince said: "I offended and came here; fortunately I was spared—how dare I act rashly!
translations.idiomatic: The prince said: "I offended and was sent here. I was spared. How dare I act rashly!

sentences.zh: 且太后有詔，便應官屬來，何獨使汝也？

translations.literal: Moreover, if the empress dowager had an edict, officials should have come—why send you alone?
translations.idiomatic: And if the empress dowager had an edict, officials would have come. Why send you alone?

sentences.zh: 汝必為亂！」

translations.literal: You are sure to make trouble!"
translations.idiomatic: You are bound to make trouble!"

sentences.zh: 因叱左右縛之，龍懼而走。

translations.literal: He then shouted to his attendants to bind him; Long, in fear, fled.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered his attendants to seize him. Xu Long fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 甲午，悚帥眾三百人，晨攻廣莫門。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Song led three hundred men and at dawn attacked the Gate of Broad Darkness.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Lu Song led three hundred followers in a dawn assault on the Gate of Broad Darkness.

sentences.zh: 詐稱海西公還，由雲龍門突入殿庭，略取武庫甲仗，門下吏士駭愕不知所為。

translations.literal: Falsely claiming the Prince of Haixi had returned, they burst through the Cloud-Dragon Gate into the palace courtyard, seized arms and armor from the arsenal, and the gate officials and guards were struck with terror and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming falsely that the Prince of Haixi was returning, they rushed through the Cloud-Dragon Gate into the palace court, looted the armory, and the gate officials and guards stood stunned, not knowing what to do.

sentences.zh: 游擊將軍毛安之聞難，帥眾直入雲龍門，手自奮擊；

translations.literal: Mobile Corps General Mao Anzhi, hearing of the crisis, led his troops straight through the Cloud-Dragon Gate and fought fiercely in person;
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Corps General Mao Anzhi, hearing of the attack, led his men straight through the Cloud-Dragon Gate and fought hand to hand himself;

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍殷康，中領軍桓秘入止車門，與安之並力討誅之，並黨與死者數百人。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Yin Kang and Central Army Commander Huan Mi entered by the Gate Where Chariots Stop and, joining forces with Anzhi, attacked and killed them; their followers who died numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Yin Kang and Central Army Commander Huan Mi entered through the Gate Where Chariots Stop and, together with Anzhi, put the rebels down. Several hundred of their followers were killed.

sentences.zh: 海西公深慮橫禍，專飲酒，恣聲色，有子為育，時人憐之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Haixi, deeply fearing sudden disaster, devoted himself to drinking and indulged freely in music and women; he had a son named Yu, and people of the time pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Haixi lived in constant fear of violent death. He drank constantly and gave himself over to pleasure. He had a son named Yu, and contemporaries pitied him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其安於屈辱，故不復為虞。

translations.literal: The court, because he seemed resigned to humiliation, no longer regarded him as a threat.
translations.idiomatic: The court assumed he had accepted his humiliation and no longer worried about him.

sentences.zh: 秦都督北蕃諸軍事、鎮北大將軍、開府儀同三司、朔方桓侯梁平老卒。

translations.literal: Liang Pinglao, Marquis Huan of Shuofang, Governor of military affairs in the northern frontier regions of Qin, Grand General Who Pacifies the North, and Bearer of an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies, died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Pinglao, Former Qin's commander on the northern frontier, Grand General Who Pacifies the North, and Marquis Huan of Shuofang, died.

sentences.zh: 平老在鎮十餘年，鮮卑、匈奴憚而愛之。

translations.literal: Pinglao had been stationed on the frontier for more than ten years; the Xianbei and Xiongnu both feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglao had held the frontier command for more than ten years, and the Xianbei and Xiongnu both feared and admired him.

sentences.zh: 三吳大旱，饑，人多餓死。

translations.literal: The Three Wu regions suffered a great drought and famine; many people starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Wu regions suffered severe drought and famine, and many people died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，己丑朔，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day jichou, the first of the month, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the new moon of jichou, the court proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the reign era.

sentences.zh: 二月，大司馬溫來朝。

translations.literal: In the second month, Grand Marshal Wen came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Grand Marshal Huan Wen came to court.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔吏部尚書謝安、侍中王坦之迎於新亭。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, an edict ordered Minister of the Civil Service Xie An and Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi to welcome him at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, the court ordered Minister of the Civil Service Xie An and Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi to welcome him at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 是時，都下人情恟恟，或雲欲誅王、謝，因移晉室。

translations.literal: At that time popular feeling in the capital was agitated; some said Wen meant to execute the Wang and Xie families and thereby displace the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors swept the capital. Some said Huan Wen intended to kill the Wang and Xie clans and seize the throne for himself.

sentences.zh: 坦之甚懼，安神色不變，曰：「晉祚存亡，決於此行。」

translations.literal: Tanzhi was greatly afraid, but An's expression did not change. He said: "The survival or fall of the Jin dynasty will be decided on this journey."
translations.idiomatic: Tanzhi was terrified, but Xie An's face did not change. He said, "The fate of the Jin dynasty rests on this journey."

sentences.zh: 溫既至，百官拜於道側。

translations.literal: When Wen arrived, the officials bowed along the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen arrived, officials lined the road and bowed.

sentences.zh: 溫大陳兵衛，延見朝士，有位望者皆戰懾失色，坦之流汗沾衣，倒執手版。

translations.literal: Wen arrayed a great guard of troops and received the court gentlemen; those of rank and standing all trembled in fear and changed color. Tanzhi sweated until his clothes were soaked and held his tablet upside down.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen displayed a massive armed escort and summoned the court gentlemen to an audience. Men of standing trembled and went pale. Tanzhi sweated through his robes and held his official tablet upside down.

sentences.zh: 安從容就席，坐定，謂溫曰：「安聞諸侯有道，守在四鄰，明公何須壁後置人邪！」

translations.literal: An took his seat at ease; when he was settled, he said to Wen: "I have heard that when feudal lords follow the Way, their defense lies in the four neighboring states—why must Your Excellency place men behind the screen!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie An took his seat calmly. When he was settled, he said to Huan Wen, "I have heard that when a lord follows the Way, his defense lies with his neighbors. Why must Your Excellency keep armed men behind the screen!"

sentences.zh: 溫笑曰：「正自不能不爾。」

translations.literal: Wen smiled and said: "Truly, I could not do otherwise."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen smiled and said, "I truly could not help it."

sentences.zh: 遂命左右撤之，與安笑語移日。

translations.literal: He then ordered his attendants to remove them and talked and laughed with An until the day was nearly spent.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the armed men withdrawn and talked and laughed with Xie An until sunset.

sentences.zh: 郗超常為溫謀主，安與坦之見溫，溫使超臥帳中聽其言。

translations.literal: Chi Chao had long been Wen's chief strategist. When An and Tanzhi visited Wen, Wen had Chao lie hidden in the tent to listen to their words.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Chao had long been Huan Wen's chief strategist. When Xie An and Wang Tanzhi came to see him, Huan Wen had Chao hide in the tent to eavesdrop.

sentences.zh: 風動帳開，安笑曰：「郗生可謂入幕之賓矣。」

translations.literal: The wind stirred the tent open, and An smiled and said: "Master Chi may truly be called a guest who has entered the tent."
translations.idiomatic: A gust of wind blew the tent open. Xie An smiled and said, "Master Chi is truly a guest who has entered the tent."

sentences.zh: 時天子幼弱，外有強臣，安與坦之盡忠輔衛，卒安晉室。

translations.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven was young and weak and there was a powerful minister abroad; An and Tanzhi served loyally as protectors and in the end secured the Jin house.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still a child, and a powerful minister held the realm in his grip. Xie An and Wang Tanzhi served loyally as protectors and in the end preserved the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 溫治盧悚入宮事，收尚書陸始付廷尉，免桓秘官，連坐者甚眾；

translations.literal: Wen investigated Lu Song's intrusion into the palace, arrested Minister of the Masters of Writing Lu Shi and handed him over to the Court of Justice, removed Huan Mi from office, and very many were implicated;
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen investigated Lu Song's palace raid, arrested Minister of the Masters of Writing Lu Shi and turned him over to the Court of Justice, stripped Huan Mi of his post, and implicated a great many others;

sentences.zh: 遷毛安之為右衛將軍，桓秘由是怨溫。

translations.literal: Mao Anzhi was transferred to be Right Guard General, and because of this Huan Mi resented Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Anzhi was made Right Guard General, and Huan Mi came to resent Huan Wen for it.

sentences.zh: 三月，溫有疾，停建康十四日，甲午，還姑孰。

translations.literal: In the third month Wen fell ill, remained at Jiankang fourteen days, and on the day jiawu returned to Gudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Huan Wen fell ill. He stayed at Jiankang fourteen days, then on jiawu returned to Gudu.

sentences.zh: 夏，代王什翼犍使燕鳳入貢於秦。

translations.literal: In summer, King Shiyijian of Dai sent Yan Feng to present tribute to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, King Shiyijian of Dai sent Yan Feng to offer tribute to Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己亥，南郡宣武公桓溫薨。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day jihai, Duke Xuanwu of Nandun, Huan Wen, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on jihai, Duke Xuanwu of Nandun, Huan Wen, died.

sentences.zh: 初，溫疾篤，諷朝廷求九錫，屢使人趣之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen's illness was grave, he hinted to the court that he sought the Nine Bestowals and repeatedly sent men to press for them.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen's illness turned grave, he pressed the court for the Nine Bestowals and sent messenger after messenger to hurry them along.

sentences.zh: 謝安、王坦之故緩其事，使袁宏具草。

translations.literal: Xie An and Wang Tanzhi deliberately delayed the matter and had Yuan Hong prepare a draft.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An and Wang Tanzhi deliberately stalled and had Yuan Hong draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 宏以示王彪之，彪之歎其文辭之美，因曰：「卿固大才，安可以此示人！」

translations.literal: Hong showed it to Wang Biaozhi; Biaozhi sighed at the beauty of its wording and then said: "You are indeed a man of great talent—how can you show this to others!"
translations.idiomatic: Hong showed the draft to Wang Biaozhi. Biaozhi admired its eloquence, then said, "You are a man of great talent. You must not let others see this!"

sentences.zh: 謝安見其草，輒改之，由是歷旬不就。

translations.literal: When Xie An saw the draft, he altered it each time, and so more than ten days passed without completion.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Xie An saw the draft, he revised it, and more than ten days passed without a finished document.

sentences.zh: 宏密謀於彪之，彪之曰：「聞彼病日增，亦當不復支久，自可更小遲回。」

translations.literal: Hong secretly consulted Biaozhi, and Biaozhi said: "I hear his illness grows daily; he surely cannot hold out much longer. We can naturally delay a little longer."
translations.idiomatic: Hong consulted Biaozhi in private. Biaozhi said, "I hear his illness grows worse by the day. He cannot last much longer. We can afford to delay a little longer."

sentences.zh: 宏從之。

translations.literal: Hong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Hong took his advice.

sentences.zh: 溫弟江州刺史沖，問溫以謝安、王坦之所任，溫曰：「渠等不為汝所處分。」

translations.literal: Wen's younger brother Chong, Governor of Jiangzhou, asked Wen about the appointments of Xie An and Wang Tanzhi. Wen said: "Those men are not for you to dispose of."
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen's younger brother Chong, governor of Jiangzhou, asked him about the appointments of Xie An and Wang Tanzhi. Huan Wen said, "Those men are not yours to remove."

sentences.zh: 其意以為，己存，彼必不敢立異，死則非沖所制；

translations.literal: His meaning was that while he lived, they would surely not dare oppose him, but after his death they would not be under Chong's control;
translations.idiomatic: He meant that while he lived, they would not dare defy him, but after his death they would be beyond Chong's control;

sentences.zh: 若害之，無益於沖，更失時望故也。

translations.literal: if they were harmed, it would do Chong no good and would only cost him public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: and if Chong harmed them, it would do him no good and would only cost him public esteem.

sentences.zh: 溫以世子熙才弱，使沖領其眾。

translations.literal: Wen, because his heir Xi was weak in talent, had Chong lead his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen judged his heir Xi too weak and had Chong take command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 於是桓秘與熙弟濟謀共殺沖，沖密知之，不敢入。

translations.literal: Thereupon Huan Mi and Xi's younger brother Ji plotted together to kill Chong; Chong learned of it in secret and did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Mi and Xi's younger brother Ji then plotted to kill Chong. Chong learned of it secretly and did not dare enter.

sentences.zh: 俄頃，溫薨，沖先遣力士拘錄熙、濟而後臨喪。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Wen died; Chong first sent strongmen to seize and arrest Xi and Ji, and only then attended the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Huan Wen died. Chong first sent strongmen to seize Xi and Ji, then attended the funeral.

sentences.zh: 秘遂被廢棄，熙、濟俱徙長沙。

translations.literal: Mi was then dismissed from office, and both Xi and Ji were banished to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was stripped of office, and both Xi and Ji were exiled to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 詔葬溫依漢霍光及安平獻王故事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Wen be buried according to the precedents of Huo Guang of Han and the King Xian of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Huan Wen buried with the honors given Huo Guang of Han and King Xian of Anping.

sentences.zh: 沖稱溫遺命，以少子玄為嗣，時方五歲，襲封南郡公。

translations.literal: Chong declared it Wen's dying command that his youngest son Xuan be made heir; Xuan was then only five years old and inherited the title Duke of Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: Chong declared it Huan Wen's dying wish that his youngest son Xuan succeed him. Xuan was only five and inherited the title Duke of Nandun.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，加右將軍、荊州刺史桓豁征西將軍，督荊、楊、雍、交、廣五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Right General and Governor of Jingzhou Huan Huo was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the West and made Overseer of military affairs in Jing, Yang, Yong, Jiao, and Guang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Right General and Jingzhou governor Huan Huo was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and overseer of military affairs in Jing, Yang, Yong, Jiao, and Guang.

sentences.zh: 以江州刺史桓沖為中軍將軍、都督揚、豫、江三州諸軍事、揚、豫二州刺史，鎮姑孰；

translations.literal: Huan Chong, Governor of Jiangzhou, was made Central Army General, Commander of military affairs in Yang, Yu, and Jiang provinces, and Governor of Yang and Yu, stationed at Gudu;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhou governor Huan Chong was made Central Army General, commander of military affairs in Yang, Yu, and Jiang, and governor of Yang and Yu, stationed at Gudu;

sentences.zh: 竟陵太守桓石秀為寧遠將軍、江州刺史，鎮尋陽。

translations.literal: Huan Shixiu, Administrator of Jingling, was made Pacifying-the-Distance General and Governor of Jiangzhou, stationed at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jingling prefect Huan Shixiu was made Pacifying-the-Distance General and governor of Jiangzhou, stationed at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 石秀，豁之子也。

translations.literal: Shixiu was the son of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Shixiu was a son of Huan Huo.

sentences.zh: 沖既代溫居任，盡忠王室，或勸沖誅除時望，專執時權，沖不從。

translations.literal: Once Chong had replaced Wen in office, he served the royal house loyally; some urged him to eliminate men of public standing and monopolize power, but Chong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chong succeeded Huan Wen, he served the throne loyally. Some urged him to purge men of standing and seize power for himself, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 始，溫在鎮，死罪皆專決不請。

translations.literal: At first, when Wen was stationed on the frontier, capital cases were all decided by him alone without requesting approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen held frontier command, he decided capital cases on his own without seeking court approval.

sentences.zh: 沖以為生殺之重，當歸朝廷，凡大辟皆先上，須報，然後行之。

translations.literal: Chong held that the power of life and death should belong to the court; all capital sentences were first submitted upward, and only after approval was received were they carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chong held that the power of life and death belonged to the court. All capital sentences had to be reported to the capital and carried out only after approval.

sentences.zh: 謝安以天子幼沖，新喪元輔，欲請崇德太后臨朝。

translations.literal: Xie An, because the Son of Heaven was young and the chief minister had just died, wished to ask Empress Dowager Chongde to hold court.
translations.idiomatic: With the emperor still a child and the chief minister newly dead, Xie An wanted Empress Dowager Chongde to hold court.

sentences.zh: 王彪之曰：「前世人主幼在襁褓，母子一體，故可臨朝；

translations.literal: Wang Biaozhi said: "In former times, when rulers were infants in swaddling clothes, mother and son were one body, and so regency was possible;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Biaozhi said, "In earlier times, when an emperor was still in swaddling clothes, mother and son were one body, so regency was possible;

sentences.zh: 太后亦不能決事，要須顧問大臣。

translations.literal: even so the empress dowager could not decide affairs herself and had to consult the great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: even then the empress dowager could not decide affairs on her own and had to rely on the great ministers.

sentences.zh: 今上年出十歲，垂及冠婚，反令從嫂臨朝，示人君幼弱，豈所以光揚聖德乎！

translations.literal: Now His Majesty is past ten years of age and nearly at the age of capping and marriage; to have a sister-in-law hold court instead would show the ruler as weak—how could that glorify imperial virtue!
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty is already past ten and nearing the age of capping and marriage. To have a sister-in-law hold court would show the throne as weak. How would that glorify imperial virtue!

sentences.zh: 諸公必欲行此，豈僕所制，所惜者大體耳。」

translations.literal: If you gentlemen insist on this course, it is not within my power to stop you; what I regret is only the damage to the larger principle."
translations.idiomatic: If you gentlemen insist on this, I cannot stop you. What I regret is the damage to the larger principle."

sentences.zh: 安不欲委任桓沖，故使太后臨朝，己得以專獻替裁決，遂不從彪之之言。

translations.literal: An did not wish to entrust authority to Huan Chong, and so had the empress dowager hold court so that he himself could monopolize proposals and decisions; he therefore did not follow Biaozhi's advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An did not want to entrust power to Huan Chong. He had the empress dowager hold court so he could control policy himself, and he ignored Biaozhi's advice.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子，太后復臨朝懾政。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day renzi, the empress dowager again held court and governed as regent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, the empress dowager resumed holding court as regent.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史楊亮遣其子廣襲仇池，與秦梁州刺史楊安戰，廣兵敗，沮水諸戌皆委城奔潰。

translations.literal: Yang Liang, Governor of Liangzhou, sent his son Guang to raid Chouchi; he fought Qin's Governor of Liangzhou Yang An, Guang's army was defeated, and the garrisons along the Ju River all abandoned their cities and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou governor Yang Liang sent his son Guang to raid Chouchi. Guang fought Former Qin's Liangzhou governor Yang An and was defeated. The garrisons along the Ju River abandoned their posts and fled.

sentences.zh: 亮懼，退守磬險。

translations.literal: Liang, in fear, withdrew and held Panxian.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Yang Liang withdrew to Panxian.

sentences.zh: 九月，安進攻漢川。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, An advanced to attack Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Yang An advanced against Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以王彪之為尚書令，謝安為僕射，領吏部，共掌朝政。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Wang Biaozhi was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xie An was made Vice Director, concurrently heading the Ministry of the Civil Service; together they controlled court governance.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Wang Biaozhi was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Xie An Vice Director with charge of the Ministry of the Civil Service. Together they governed the court.

sentences.zh: 安每歎曰：「朝廷大事，眾所不能決者，以咨王公，無不立決。」

translations.literal: An often sighed and said: "On great affairs of state that the multitude cannot decide, once I consult Lord Wang, there is none that is not settled at once."
translations.idiomatic: Xie An often said with a sigh, "On great affairs of state that no one else can settle, once I consult Lord Wang, the matter is decided at once."

sentences.zh: 以吳國內史刁彝為徐、兗二州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: Diao Yi, Interior Minister of Wu, was made Governor of Xu and Yan provinces and stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yi, interior minister of Wu, was made governor of Xu and Yan and posted at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 冬，秦王堅使益州刺史王統、秘書監朱肜帥卒二萬出漢川，前禁將軍毛當、鷹揚將軍徐成帥卒三萬出劍門，入寇梁、益；

translations.literal: In winter, King Fu Jian of Qin sent Wang Tong, Governor of Yizhou, and Zhu Rong, Director of the Masters of Writing, leading twenty thousand troops out from Hanchuan, and Forward Prohibitions General Mao Dang and Soaring-Hawk General Xu Cheng leading thirty thousand troops out from Jianmen, to invade Liang and Yi;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, King Fu Jian sent Yizhou governor Wang Tong and Director of the Masters of Writing Zhu Rong with twenty thousand men from Hanchuan, and Forward Prohibitions General Mao Dang and Soaring-Hawk General Xu Cheng with thirty thousand through Jianmen, to invade Liang and Yi;

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史楊亮帥巴獠萬餘拒之，戰於青谷。

translations.literal: Yang Liang, Governor of Liangzhou, led more than ten thousand Ba and Liao troops to resist them and fought at Qinggu.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou governor Yang Liang led more than ten thousand Ba and Liao troops to resist them and fought at Qinggu.

sentences.zh: 亮兵敗，奔固西城。

translations.literal: Liang's army was defeated and he fled to Guxicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Liang was defeated and fled to Guxicheng.

sentences.zh: 肜遂拔漢中。

translations.literal: Rong then captured Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Rong then took Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 徐成攻劍門，克之。

translations.literal: Xu Cheng attacked Jianmen and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cheng attacked Jianmen and took it.

sentences.zh: 楊安進攻梓潼，梓潼太守周颺固守涪城，遣步騎數千送母、妻自漢水趣江陵，朱肜邀而獲之，颺遂降於安。

translations.literal: Yang An advanced to attack Zitong; Zhou Yang, Administrator of Zitong, held firm at Fucheng and sent several thousand infantry and cavalry to escort his mother and wife from the Han River toward Jiangling. Zhu Rong intercepted and captured them, and Yang then surrendered to An.
translations.idiomatic: Yang An advanced on Zitong. Zitong prefect Zhou Yang held Fucheng and sent several thousand foot and horse to escort his mother and wife down the Han toward Jiangling. Zhu Rong intercepted them, and Zhou Yang surrendered to Yang An.

sentences.zh: 十一月，安克梓潼。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, An captured Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Yang An took Zitong.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史桓豁遣江夏相竺瑤救梁、益；

translations.literal: Huan Huo, Governor of Jingzhou, sent Zhu Yao, Administrator of Jiangxia, to relieve Liang and Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou governor Huan Huo sent Jiangxia prefect Zhu Yao to relieve Liang and Yi;

sentences.zh: 瑤聞廣漢太守趙長戰死，引兵退。

translations.literal: Yao, hearing that Zhao Chang, Administrator of Guanghan, had died in battle, withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yao heard that Guanghan prefect Zhao Chang had fallen in battle, he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史周仲孫勒兵拒朱肜於綿竹，聞毛當將至成都，仲孫帥騎五千奔於南中。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhongsun, Governor of Yizhou, mustered troops to resist Zhu Rong at Mianzhu; hearing that Mao Dang was about to reach Chengdu, Zhongsun led five thousand cavalry and fled to the Southern Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou governor Zhou Zhongsun mustered troops to resist Zhu Rong at Mianzhu. When he heard Mao Dang was nearing Chengdu, he fled south with five thousand cavalry.

sentences.zh: 奉遂取梁、益二州，邛、莋、夜郎皆附於秦。

translations.literal: Qin then took the two provinces of Liang and Yi; Qiong, Zuo, and Yelang all submitted to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin then seized Liang and Yi. Qiong, Zuo, and Yelang all submitted to Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅以楊安為益州牧，鎮成都；

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin made Yang An Governor-General of Yizhou and stationed him at Chengdu;
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian made Yang An governor-general of Yizhou and posted him at Chengdu;

sentences.zh: 毛當為州刺史，鎮漢中；

translations.literal: Mao Dang was made Governor of Liangzhou and stationed at Hanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dang was made governor of Liangzhou and posted at Hanzhong;

sentences.zh: 姚萇為寧州刺史，屯墊江；

translations.literal: Yao Chang was made Governor of Ningzhou and encamped at Dianjiang;
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang was made governor of Ningzhou and encamped at Dianjiang;

sentences.zh: 王統為南秦州刺史，鎮仇池。

translations.literal: Wang Tong was made Governor of Southern Qinzhou and stationed at Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tong was made governor of Southern Qinzhou and posted at Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅欲以周虓為尚書郎。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin wished to appoint Zhou Jiao as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian wished to appoint Zhou Jiao as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 虓曰：「蒙晉厚恩，但老母見獲，失節於此，母子獲全，秦之惠也。

translations.literal: Jiao said: "I received great favor from Jin, but my aged mother was captured, and I lost my integrity here. That mother and son were both spared is Qin's kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao said, "Jin showed me great kindness, but my mother was captured and I lost my integrity here. That we were both spared is Former Qin's mercy.

sentences.zh: 雖公侯之貴，不以為榮，況郎官乎！」

translations.literal: Even the honor of duke or marquis I would not take as glory—how much less a Gentleman's post!"
translations.idiomatic: Even a duke's or marquis's rank would not honor me. How much less a clerk's post!"

sentences.zh: 遂不仕。

translations.literal: He therefore would not serve.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to serve.

sentences.zh: 每見堅，或箕踞而坐，呼為氐賊。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw Fu Jian, he sometimes sat with legs sprawled and called him "Di bandit."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw Fu Jian, he sometimes sat sprawled with legs apart and called him "Di bandit."

sentences.zh: 嘗值元會，儀衛甚盛，堅問之曰：「晉朝元會，與此何如？」

translations.literal: Once, on the New Year's court assembly, the guard of honor was very grand. Fu Jian asked him: "How does the Jin court's New Year's assembly compare with this?"
translations.idiomatic: Once at the New Year's court assembly, when the guard of honor was at its grandest, Fu Jian asked him, "How does the Eastern Jin New Year's assembly compare with this?"

sentences.zh: 虓攘袂厲聲曰：「犬羊相聚，何敢比擬天朝！」

translations.literal: Jiao rolled up his sleeves and said in a fierce voice: "Dogs and sheep gathered together—how dare they be compared with the Celestial Court!"
translations.idiomatic: Jiao rolled up his sleeves and shouted, "Dogs and sheep huddled together! How dare they compare themselves with the Celestial Court!"

sentences.zh: 秦人以虓不遜，屢請殺之，堅待之彌厚。

translations.literal: The people of Qin, because Jiao was insolent, repeatedly asked that he be killed, but Fu Jian treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Qin officials, finding Jiao insolent, repeatedly asked Fu Jian to kill him, but he treated Jiao all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 周仲孫坐失守免官。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhongsun was removed from office for losing his command.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhongsun was stripped of office for losing his province.

sentences.zh: 桓沖以冠軍將軍毛虎生為益州刺史，領建平太守，以虎生子球為梓潼太守。

translations.literal: Huan Chong made Mao Husheng, Champion General, Governor of Yizhou and acting Administrator of Jianping, and made Husheng's son Qiu Administrator of Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong made Champion General Mao Husheng governor of Yizhou and acting prefect of Jianping, and appointed Husheng's son Qiu prefect of Zitong.

sentences.zh: 虎生與球代秦，至巴西，以糧乏，退屯巴東。

translations.literal: Husheng and Qiu replaced Qin and advanced as far as Baxi, but because supplies ran short, they withdrew and encamped at Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Husheng and Qiu marched to recover the territory from Qin and reached Baxi, but short of supplies they fell back to Badong.

sentences.zh: 以侍中王坦之為中書令，領丹楊尹。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi was made Director of the Masters of Writing in the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Magistrate of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wang Tanzhi was made Director of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently magistrate of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 是歲，鮮卑勃寒寇掠隴右，秦王堅使乞伏司繁討之。

translations.literal: That year the Xianbei chief Bohán raided Longyou; King Fu Jian of Qin sent Qifu Sifan to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Xianbei chief Bohán raided Longyou. King Fu Jian sent Qifu Sifan against him.

sentences.zh: 勃寒請降，遂使司繁鎮勇士川。

translations.literal: Bohán requested surrender, and Sifan was then stationed to guard Yongshi River.
translations.idiomatic: Bohán surrendered, and Qifu Sifan was posted to guard Yongshi River.

sentences.zh: 有彗星出於尾箕，長十餘丈，經太微，掃東井；

translations.literal: A comet appeared from Tail and Winnowing Basket, more than ten zhang in length, passed through Supreme Palace Enclosure, and swept Eastern Well;
translations.idiomatic: A comet appeared from the Tail and Winnowing Basket asterisms, more than ten zhang long, passed through the Supreme Palace Enclosure, and swept the Eastern Well;

sentences.zh: 自四月始見，及秋冬不滅。

translations.literal: It was first seen from the fourth month and did not fade through autumn and winter.
translations.idiomatic: It first appeared in the fourth month and remained visible through autumn and winter.

sentences.zh: 秦太史令張孟言於秦王堅曰：「尾、箕，燕分；

translations.literal: Zhang Meng, Grand Astrologer of Qin, said to King Fu Jian of Qin: "Tail and Winnowing Basket are Yan's allotted region;
translations.idiomatic: Qin Grand Astrologer Zhang Meng told King Fu Jian, "Tail and Winnowing Basket belong to Yan's allotted region;

sentences.zh: 東井，秦分也。

translations.literal: Eastern Well is Qin's allotted region.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Well is Qin's allotted region.

sentences.zh: 令彗起尾、箕而掃東井，十年之後，燕當滅秦；

translations.literal: Now the comet rises from Tail and Winnowing Basket and sweeps Eastern Well—in ten years Yan will destroy Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Now the comet rises from Tail and Winnowing Basket and sweeps Eastern Well. In ten years Yan will destroy Qin;

sentences.zh: 二十年之後，代當滅燕。

translations.literal: in twenty years Dai will destroy Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In twenty years Dai will destroy Yan.

sentences.zh: 慕容□父子兄弟，我之仇敵，而布列朝廷，貴盛莫二，臣竊憂之，宜翦其抱魁桀者，以消天變。」

translations.literal: Murong Chui, his sons, and his brothers are our enemy foes, yet they are arrayed throughout the court, in honor and splendor second to none. Your subject privately fears this; we ought to cut down the ringleaders among them to dispel the celestial anomaly."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui and his sons and brothers are our sworn enemies, yet they fill the court ranks, second to none in rank and power. I am deeply troubled. Cut down their leading men and Heaven's warning may be averted."

sentences.zh: 堅不聽。

translations.literal: Fu Jian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian would not listen.

sentences.zh: 陽平公融上疏曰：「東胡跨據六州，南面稱帝，陛下勞師累年，然後得之，本非慕義而來。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yangping, Rong, submitted a memorial saying: "The Eastern Hu held six provinces and styled themselves emperors facing south. Your Majesty exhausted the army for years before taking them—they did not come out of admiration for righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Yangping, Fu Rong, submitted a memorial: "The Eastern Hu held six provinces and called themselves emperors in the south. Your Majesty wore out the army for years before conquering them. They did not submit out of love for righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今陛下親而幸之，使其父子兄弟森然滿朝，執權履職，勢傾勳舊。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty treats them with personal favor, so that fathers, sons, and brothers stand thick throughout the court, wielding power and filling offices, their influence eclipsing the meritorious elders.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty favors them as kin, and their fathers, sons, and brothers stand rank upon rank in court, wielding office and power until they overshadow the old servants of merit.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為狼虎之心，終不可養，星變如此，願少留意。」

translations.literal: This subject thinks the heart of a wolf or tiger can never truly be raised. With the stars changing thus, I beg Your Majesty to give it some attention."
translations.idiomatic: I am convinced that a wolf's or tiger's heart can never be kept fed in safety. The heavens show such a sign—please give this some heed."

sentences.zh: 堅報曰：「朕方混六合為一家，視夷狄為赤子。

translations.literal: Fu Jian replied: "I am now merging the Six Directions into one household, treating the barbarians as my own newborn children.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian answered: "I mean to fuse the six quarters of the realm into one household and count the alien peoples as my own infant children.

sentences.zh: 汝宜息慮，勿懷耿介。

translations.literal: You should lay your cares to rest and not hold such stubborn scruples.
translations.idiomatic: Set your mind at ease and do not cling to such rigid scruples.

sentences.zh: 夫惟修德可以禳災，苟能內求諸己，何懼外患乎！」

translations.literal: Only cultivating virtue can avert calamity. If one can seek within oneself, what need to fear external trouble!"
translations.idiomatic: Only by cultivating virtue can disaster be turned aside. If a man looks within himself, what external threat need he dread?"

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸未朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guwei the new moon, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the new moon of the first month, day guwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 己酉，刁彝卒。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Diao Yi died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Diao Yi died.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸丑，以王坦之為都督徐、兗、青三州諸軍事、徐、兗二州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guichou, Wang Tanzhi was made Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces and Governor of Xu and Yan, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, Wang Tanzhi was made commander of military affairs in Xu, Yan, and Qing and governor of Xu and Yan, with his seat at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 詔謝安總中書。

translations.literal: An edict put Xie An in overall charge of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed Xie An in overall charge of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 安好聲律，期功之慘，不廢絲竹，士大夫效之，遂以成俗。

translations.literal: An loved music and tonal rules; even amid the deepest mourning for deceased relatives he would not put aside his lutes and pipes. The gentry scholars took this as a model, and it became custom.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An loved music and tonal refinement. Even in the deepest mourning for a kinsman he would not lay aside his strings and pipes. The gentry took him as their model, and the practice hardened into custom.

sentences.zh: 王坦之屢以書苦諫之曰：「天下之寶，當為天下惜之。」

translations.literal: Wang Tanzhi repeatedly wrote bitter admonitions saying: "The treasures of the realm ought to be cherished for the realm's sake."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi wrote again and again in bitter remonstrance: "The treasures of the realm should be treasured for the realm's sake."

sentences.zh: 安不能從。

translations.literal: An could not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦太尉建寧列公李威卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, Li Wei, Grand Commandant and Duke of Jianninglie of Qin, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Li Wei, Qin grand commandant and Duke of Jianninglie, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，蜀人張育、楊光起兵擊秦，有眾二萬，遣使來請兵。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, the Shu men Zhang Yu and Yang Guang raised troops to attack Qin with twenty thousand followers and sent envoys to request reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, the Shu leaders Zhang Yu and Yang Guang took up arms against Qin with twenty thousand men and sent envoys to Jin asking for troops.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅遣鎮軍將軍鄧羌帥甲士五萬討之。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian of Qin sent Pacifying Army General Deng Qiang leading fifty thousand armored troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian sent Pacifying Army General Deng Qiang with fifty thousand armored troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史竺瑤、威遠將軍桓石虔帥眾三萬攻墊江，姚萇兵敗，退屯五城。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Zhu Yao and Might-reaching General Huan Shiqian led thirty thousand troops to attack Dianjiang; Yao Chang's army was defeated and withdrew to encamp at Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou inspector Zhu Yao and Might-reaching General Huan Shiqian marched thirty thousand men against Dianjiang. Yao Chang was routed and fell back to Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 瑤、石虔屯巴東。

translations.literal: Yao and Shiqian encamped at Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yao and Huan Shiqian encamped at Badong.

sentences.zh: 張育自號蜀王，與巴獠酋帥張重、尹萬等五萬餘人進圍成都。

translations.literal: Zhang Yu styled himself King of Shu and, together with the Ba-Liao chieftains Zhang Chong, Yin Wan, and others—more than fifty thousand men—advanced to besiege Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu declared himself King of Shu and, with the Ba and Liao chieftains Zhang Chong, Yin Wan, and more than fifty thousand followers, pressed the siege of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 六月，育改元黑龍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yu changed the era name to Black Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zhang Yu proclaimed the era name Black Dragon.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，張育與張重等爭權，舉兵相攻，秦楊安、鄧羌襲育，敗之，育與楊光退屯綿竹。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Yu and Zhang Chong and the others contended for power and raised troops against each other. Qin generals Yang An and Deng Qiang attacked Yu by surprise, defeated him, and Yu and Yang Guang withdrew to encamp at Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhang Yu and Zhang Chong fell out over power and turned their armies on each other. Yang An and Deng Qiang of Qin struck Yu by surprise, routed him, and Yu and Yang Guang retreated to Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 八月，鄧羌敗晉兵於涪西。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Deng Qiang defeated Jin troops west of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Deng Qiang defeated Jin forces west of Fu.

sentences.zh: 九月，楊安敗張重、尹萬於成都南，重死，斬首二萬三千級。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yang An defeated Zhang Chong and Yin Wan south of Chengdu; Chong died, and twenty-three thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Yang An routed Zhang Chong and Yin Wan south of Chengdu. Chong was killed, and twenty-three thousand heads were counted.

sentences.zh: 鄧羌擊張育、楊光於綿竹，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Deng Qiang attacked Zhang Yu and Yang Guang at Mianzhu and beheaded them both.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Qiang struck Zhang Yu and Yang Guang at Mianzhu and beheaded them both.

sentences.zh: 益州復入於秦。

translations.literal: Yizhou again came under Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou again passed back under Qin control.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，有人入秦明光殿大呼曰：「甲申、乙酉，魚羊食人，悲哉無復遺！」

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, a man entered the Qin Mingguang Hall and shouted: "On jiashen and yiyou, fish and sheep devour men—how pitiful, none left behind!"
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, a man burst into Qin's Mingguang Hall and cried: "On jiashen and yiyou, fish and sheep will devour men—wretched, not one left alive!"

sentences.zh: 秦王堅命執之，不獲。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian ordered him seized, but he was not caught.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian ordered him seized, but he could not be found.

sentences.zh: 秘書監朱肜、秘書侍郎略陽趙整固請誅諸鮮卑，堅不聽。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Zhu Rong and Secretariat Gentleman Zhao Zheng of Lueyang repeatedly pressed for the execution of all Xianbei; Fu Jian would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Zhu Rong and Secretariat Gentleman Zhao Zheng of Lueyang urgently petitioned that all Xianbei be put to death. Fu Jian refused.

sentences.zh: 整，宦官也，博聞強記，能屬文，好直言，上書及面諫，前後五十餘事。

translations.literal: Zheng was a eunuch, broadly learned with a strong memory, able to compose prose, and fond of plain speaking; in memorials and face-to-face remonstrances there were more than fifty such occasions in all.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was a eunuch, widely read with a formidable memory, able to write polished prose, and fond of blunt speech. In written memorials and face-to-face remonstrance he had more than fifty such occasions.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂夫人得幸於堅，堅與之同輦游於後庭，整歌曰：「不見雀來入燕室，但見浮雲蔽白日。」

translations.literal: Murong Chui's wife had won Fu Jian's favor; Jian rode in the same carriage with her in the rear garden, and Zheng sang: "No sparrow seen entering the swallows' chamber—only drifting clouds blocking the white sun."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui's wife had won Fu Jian's favor. Jian rode with her in the same carriage in the rear garden, and Zheng sang: "No sparrow enters the swallows' hall—only drifting clouds blot out the white sun."

sentences.zh: 堅改容謝之，命夫人下輦。

translations.literal: Jian changed countenance and apologized, ordering the lady to leave the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian changed color and apologized, then ordered the lady to step down from the carriage.

sentences.zh: 是歲，代王什翼犍擊劉衛辰，南走。

translations.literal: That year, the king of Dai Shuyi Jian attacked Liu Weichen, who fled south.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the king of Dai, Shuyi Jian, attacked Liu Weichen, who fled south.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛亥，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinhai, a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on xinhai of the first month, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，丙午，藍田獻侯王坦之卒；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on bingwu, Marquis Xian of Lantian Wang Tanzhi died;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on bingwu, Marquis Xian of Lantian, Wang Tanzhi, died;

sentences.zh: 臨終與謝安、桓沖書，惟以國家為憂，言不及私。

translations.literal: At his dying hour he wrote to Xie An and Huan Chong, concerned only for the state and not touching private matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end he wrote to Xie An and Huan Chong, grieving only for the realm and saying nothing of private affairs.

sentences.zh: 桓沖以謝安素有重望，欲以揚州讓之，自求外出。

translations.literal: Huan Chong, because Xie An had long enjoyed great standing, wished to yield Yangzhou to him and sought an appointment away from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Chong, knowing Xie An's long-standing prestige, wished to yield Yangzhou to him and asked for a post away from the capital.

sentences.zh: 桓氏族黨皆以為非計，莫不扼腕苦諫，郗超亦深止之，沖皆不聽，處之澹然。

translations.literal: The entire Huan clan considered this poor policy and one and all wrung their hands in bitter counsel; Xi Chao also urgently dissuaded him, but Chong would not listen and took it with complete calm.
translations.idiomatic: The whole Huan clan thought this a mistake and wrung their hands in bitter remonstrance. Xi Chao also strongly urged him to stop. Chong would not listen and met it all with unruffled calm.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，詔以沖都督徐、豫、兗、青、揚五州諸軍事、徐州刺史，鎮京口；

translations.literal: On jiayin, an edict made Chong Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Xu, Yu, Yan, Qing, and Yang provinces and Inspector of Xuzhou, stationed at Jingkou;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, an edict made Huan Chong commander of military affairs in Xu, Yu, Yan, Qing, and Yang and inspector of Xuzhou, stationed at Jingkou;

sentences.zh: 以安領揚州刺史，並加侍中。

translations.literal: An was made Inspector of Yangzhou, both additionally receiving Palace Attendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An was made inspector of Yangzhou, and both men were given the rank of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 六月，秦清河武侯王猛寢疾，秦王堅親為之祈南、北郊及宗廟、社稷，分遣侍臣遍禱河、岳諸神。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Wang Meng, Marquis of Qinghe and Wu of Qin, fell gravely ill; King Fu Jian personally performed sacrifices at the southern and northern suburban altars and at the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain for his sake, and dispatched attendant ministers to pray broadly to the river, mountain, and other deities.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Wang Meng, Marquis Wu of Qinghe, fell gravely ill. King Fu Jian sacrificed in person at the southern and northern suburban altars, at the ancestral temple, and at the altars of soil and grain on his behalf, and sent attendant ministers to pray at rivers and mountains throughout the land.

sentences.zh: 猛疾少療，為之赦殊死以下。

translations.literal: Meng's illness eased somewhat, and on his account an amnesty was granted below the penalty of death.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng's illness eased a little, Fu Jian proclaimed an amnesty for all crimes short of capital punishment on his account.

sentences.zh: 猛上疏曰：「不圖陛下以臣之命而虧天地之德，開闢已來，未之有也。

translations.literal: Meng submitted a memorial saying: "I never imagined Your Majesty would diminish Heaven-and-Earth's virtue for the sake of my life—since the opening of the age, nothing like this has existed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng submitted a memorial: "I never dreamed Your Majesty would spend Heaven and Earth's virtue for the sake of my one life. Since the world began, nothing like this has been heard of.

sentences.zh: 臣聞報德莫如盡言，謹以垂沒之命，竊獻遺款。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that repaying kindness is best done with full candor; I respectfully, at the hour of my nearing end, venture my final loyal words.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the true repayment of kindness is plain speech. At the edge of death I venture my last loyal counsel.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，威烈振乎八荒，聲教光乎六合，九州百郡，十居其七，平燕定蜀，有如拾芥。

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty, whose martial splendor shakes the Eight Directions and whose civilizing influence shines upon the Six Directions; of the nine provinces and hundred commanderies, seven tenths are held; pacifying Yan and settling Shu were like picking up fallen stalks.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's martial glory shakes the eight directions and your civilizing radiance fills the six quarters. Of the nine provinces and hundred commanderies, seven tenths are yours. Conquering Yan and settling Shu were like picking up fallen stalks from the ground.

sentences.zh: 夫善作者不必善成，善始者不必善終，是以古先哲王，知功業之不易，戰戰兢兢，如臨深谷。

translations.literal: He who is good at beginning need not be good at finishing; he who is good at starting need not be good at ending. Thus the sage kings of old, knowing how hard achievements are to sustain, were cautious and trembling as though standing above a deep gorge.
translations.idiomatic: He who excels at founding need not excel at finishing; he who excels at beginning need not excel at the end. The sage kings of old knew how hard it is to hold an achievement, and trembled as though standing over a deep ravine.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，追蹤前聖，天下幸甚！」

translations.literal: I bow before Your Majesty, who follows in the footsteps of the former sages—great fortune for the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows in the footsteps of those sages, the realm will be blessed indeed!"

sentences.zh: 堅覽之悲慟。

translations.literal: When Jian read it he was stricken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian read it, he was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，堅親至猛第視疾，訪以後事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Jian personally went to Meng's residence to visit his illness and asked about affairs after his death.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Fu Jian went in person to Wang Meng's house to inquire after his illness and ask what should be done after his death.

sentences.zh: 猛曰：「晉雖僻處江南，然正朔相承，上下安和，臣沒之後，願勿以晉為圖。

translations.literal: Meng said: "Jin, though confined to the lands south of the Yangtze, yet maintains succession of the imperial orthodoxy; above and below are secure and harmonious. After your subject dies, I beg that you not contemplate Jin as a target.
translations.idiomatic: Meng said: "Jin may be confined to the south of the Yangtze, yet the imperial succession continues unbroken and the realm there is at peace. After I am gone, do not set your sights on Jin.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑、西羌，我之仇敵，終為人患，宜漸除之，以便社稷。」

translations.literal: The Xianbei and Western Qiang are our enemy foes; in the end they will become a calamity for men. They should gradually be eliminated for the convenience of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei and the Western Qiang are our sworn enemies. In time they will become a plague upon the realm. They should be removed little by little for the sake of the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 言終而卒。

translations.literal: Having spoken, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He finished speaking and died.

sentences.zh: 堅比斂，三臨哭，謂太子宏曰：「天不欲使吾平壹六合耶！

translations.literal: When the coffin was placed for lying in state Jian thrice came to mourn and said to Crown Prince Hong: "Does Heaven not wish me to unify the Six Directions!
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin was laid out, Fu Jian came three times to weep and said to Crown Prince Hong: "Does Heaven not mean for me to unite the six quarters of the realm!

sentences.zh: 何奪吾景略之速也！」

translations.literal: Why take Jinglue from me so swiftly!"
translations.idiomatic: Why must it snatch Jinglue from me so soon!"

sentences.zh: 葬之如漢霍光故事。

translations.literal: He was buried according to the precedent of Huo Guang in Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with the honors accorded Huo Guang in Han.

sentences.zh: 八月，癸巳，立皇後王氏，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on guisi, Empress Wang was installed and a general amnesty proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guisi, Empress Wang was installed and a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 後，濛之孫也。

translations.literal: The empress was the granddaughter of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was a granddaughter of Wang Mi.

sentences.zh: 以後父晉陵太守蘊為光祿大夫，領五兵尚書，封建昌縣侯，蘊固辭不受。

translations.literal: The empress's father Yun, Governor of Jinling, was made Grand Master for Splendor, concurrent Grand Minister of War, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang County; Yun steadfastly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's father, Wang Yun, governor of Jinling, was made Grand Master for Splendor and concurrent Grand Minister of War and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang County. Yun firmly declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝講《孝經》，始覽典和籍，延儒士。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the emperor lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, began to review canonical texts and records, and summoned Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the emperor lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety, began to read the canonical texts and archives, and invited Confucian scholars to court.

sentences.zh: 謝安薦東莞徐邈補中書捨人，每被顧問，多所匡益。

translations.literal: Xie An recommended Xu Miao of Dongguan to fill the post of Secretariat Attendant; whenever summoned for consultation he offered much corrective benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An recommended Xu Miao of Dongguan for the post of Secretariat Attendant. Whenever the emperor consulted him, his answers brought much corrective benefit.

sentences.zh: 帝或宴集，酣樂之後，好為手詔詩章以賜侍臣，或文詞率爾，所言穢雜；

translations.literal: When the emperor held banquets and, after deep revelry, liked to compose by hand edicts and verse to bestow upon attendant ministers, sometimes the diction was careless and the words coarse and disjointed;
translations.idiomatic: At banquets, once deep in wine and merriment, the emperor liked to draft edicts and poems by hand and bestow them on his attendants. Sometimes the wording was hasty and the content coarse or confused;

sentences.zh: 邈應時收斂還省刊削，皆使可觀，經帝重覽，然後出之，時議以此多邈。

translations.literal: Miao would promptly retrieve them back to the secretariat for revision and cutting, making all presentable; only after the emperor reviewed them anew would they be issued, and public opinion on this account praised Miao greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Miao would promptly take them back to the secretariat, revise and trim them until they were presentable, and only after the emperor had read them again would they be issued. Public opinion greatly praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guiyou the new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on the new moon of the tenth month, day guiyou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅下詔曰：「新喪賢輔，百司或未稱朕心，可置聽訟觀於未央南，朕五日一臨，以求民隱。

translations.literal: King Fu Jian issued an edict saying: "Having newly lost a worthy minister, the hundred offices may not yet accord with my heart. Let a Hall for Hearing Lawsuits be established south of Weiyang Palace; I shall come there every five days to seek out the people's hidden grievances.
translations.idiomatic: King Fu Jian issued an edict: "I have just lost a worthy minister, and the hundred offices may not yet suit my mind. Let a Hall for Hearing Lawsuits be built south of Weiyang Palace. I shall visit it every five days to seek out the people's hidden grievances.

sentences.zh: 今天下雖未大定，權可偃武修文，以稱武侯雅旨。

translations.literal: Though the realm is not yet fully settled, for the time being arms may be laid aside and civil culture pursued, to accord with the Marquis of Wu's lofty intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though the realm is not yet fully settled, for now we may lay aside arms and cultivate civil culture, in keeping with the Marquis of Wu's noble intent.

sentences.zh: 其增崇儒教，禁老、莊、圖讖之學，犯者棄市。」

translations.literal: Confucian teaching is to be elevated; the study of Laozi, Zhuangzi, and prognostic charts is forbidden—violators are to be executed in the market."
translations.idiomatic: Confucian teaching is to be exalted, and the study of Laozi, Zhuangzi, and prognostic charts is forbidden. Violators shall be executed in the market."

sentences.zh: 妙簡學生，太子及公侯百僚之子皆就學受業；

translations.literal: Outstanding students were carefully selected; the crown prince and the sons of dukes, marquises, and the hundred officials all went to study and receive instruction;
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding students were carefully chosen. The crown prince and the sons of dukes, marquises, and the hundred officials all entered school to receive instruction;

sentences.zh: 中外四禁、二衛、四軍長上將士，皆令受學。

translations.literal: Soldiers of the four inner guards, the two wings, and the four armies on long-term duty were all ordered to receive schooling.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men of the four inner guards, the two wings, and the four armies on long-term duty were all ordered to receive schooling.

sentences.zh: 二十人給一經生，教讀音句，後宮置典學以教掖庭，選閹人及女隸敏慧者詣博士授經。

translations.literal: Twenty men were assigned one classicist to teach reading and phrasing; within the rear palace a canonical academy was established to instruct the palace women, and eunuchs and clever serving women selected were sent to the classicists for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Every twenty men were given one classicist to teach reading and phrasing. Within the rear palace a canonical academy was set up to instruct the palace women, and clever eunuchs and serving women were chosen to receive instruction from the classicists.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎王佩讀讖，堅殺之，學讖者遂絕。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Wang Pei studied prognostic charts; Fu Jian had him executed, and students of prognostics thereafter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Wang Pei studied prognostic charts. Fu Jian had him executed, and the study of prognostics died out.
